items.text:
Walmart will let Meta’s Muse shop on its website on your behalf, allowing the AI agent to find and purchase Black Friday deals. Tomorrow, on Tuesday November 24th, the retail giant will roll out a live implementation of the Agent Gateway it announced last month, which helps AI agents find relevant products for you without sharing your purchase history, according to Walmart.
Meta Muse can do your Black Friday shopping at Walmart
The Walmart Agent Gateway is about to launch with Muse support, with other apps and agents ‘on the way.’
Muse can make purchases through Walmart’s “Agent Profiles,” which provide a dedicated space for agent activity within your Walmart customer account. These profiles also allow you to set spending limits, approve purchases, and check the purchase history of everything bought by Muse. While other online retailers like Amazon and eBay have blocked AI agents from browsing their platforms, Walmart says that support for Meta’s Muse is “just the beginning,” and that additional Walmart shopping experiences for other AI agents and apps are “on the way.”
Here are Walmart’s instructions for shopping its website via Muse:
1. Tell Muse what you need. For example, ask it to find a great TV deal or show you which Walmart Black Friday deals are available for delivery. Muse can help you explore products and build your basket.
2. Set your shopping rules. Muse will take you to Walmart to sign in, then bring you back to Muse. The first time you add an item to your cart, you’ll set up your Agent Profile on Walmart within your Walmart account, including a spending limit you’re comfortable with.
3. Check out. Complete your purchase within the conversation using a card saved in your Walmart account, with the same Walmart prices you’d find on Walmart.com. And if something isn’t quite right, Walmart’s return policy still applies.
Update, November 23rd: Walmart informed The Verge after publication that the Agent Gateway launch has been delayed by 24 hours. The ability to shop on Walmart via Muse will now be available on November 24th.

items.title: PLO Lumumba renews push for EACC prosecutorial powers to strengthen graft fight
items.summary: NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 23 – Renowned legal scholar Prof Patrick Lumumba has renewed calls for the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) to be granted prosecutorial powers, arguing that the agency’s dependence on other institutions to prosecute corruption cases undermines the effectiveness of the
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 23 – Renowned legal scholar Prof Patrick Lumumba has renewed calls for the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) to be granted prosecutorial powers, arguing that the agency’s dependence on other institutions to prosecute corruption cases undermines the effectiveness of the war against graft.
Lumumba said the decision to deny the anti-graft agency independent prosecutorial authority was deliberate, warning that the existing arrangement leaves investigators frustrated when cases they have painstakingly built encounter delays or setbacks at the prosecution stage.
He argued that allowing EACC to investigate and prosecute cases would give it greater ownership of investigations and improve the chances of successfully pursuing corruption suspects, particularly within the political class.
“People don’t want an EACC with very sharp teeth. They want an EACC that can bite and is frustrated. They will not tell you, but I’m telling you on their behalf,” Lumumba said.
Speaking during a two-day workshop for media practitioners on integrity in leadership and elections at Whitesands Beach Resort in Mombasa, the scholar recalled discussions held during the constitutional review process in which he advocated for the commission to have prosecutorial powers.
Lumumba said he and the then chairperson of the Kenya Anti-Corruption Commission had pushed for the powers during a meeting chaired by the then Prime Minister, but their proposal faced resistance from senior government officials.
He recounted that members of the working committee opposed the proposal, arguing that an empowered anti-corruption agency would become too powerful.
“They said, ‘We will make EACC a monster. We cannot allow them’,” he recalled.
Lumumba said the decision to retain a separation between investigations and prosecutions had left the commission reliant on other institutions, recalling instances when investigation files submitted to the then Attorney General were returned for further investigations.
He argued that prosecutors who take over cases at the final stage may lack the same depth of understanding and enthusiasm as investigators who have followed the evidence from the beginning.
“I can’t agree with you more, and I think it is something that when we are serious about fighting corruption, particularly the political class, give the power to prosecute and finality in some of the decisions,” he said while responding to a question posed by a journalist.
His remarks revive a longstanding debate over whether Kenya’s anti-corruption framework gives EACC sufficient authority to translate investigations into successful prosecutions.
The call comes as the country prepares for the 2027 General Election, with integrity and accountability emerging as key concerns in the vetting of political aspirants.
EACC Commissioner Col. (Rtd) Alfred Mshimba said the commission submitted integrity records of 241 individuals for consideration during the 2022 General Election, but only five were disqualified.
He questioned whether institutions were doing enough to ensure that constitutional standards on integrity and ethical leadership were enforced when Kenyans elect their leaders.
“These experiences raise an important question: Are we doing enough, as institutions and as a country, to ensure that integrity is given the attention it deserves when electing our leaders?” Mshimba posed.
He said some individuals flagged during the 2017 electoral process were subsequently arrested, charged and convicted of corruption-related offences, while others were removed from office through impeachment proceedings over violations relating to Chapter Six of the Constitution.
In a separate address delivered on his behalf by EACC Director of Investigations Paschal Mweu, Chief Executive Officer Abdi A. Mohamud said the commission would intensify integrity verification of individuals seeking elective positions ahead of the 2027 polls.
Mohamud clarified that EACC does not have the constitutional mandate to independently bar candidates from contesting elections, noting that the responsibility rests with the IEBC.
He said the commission investigates integrity concerns and submits findings and recommendations to the electoral body based on constitutional requirements and agreed verification criteria.
The CEO disclosed that EACC receives more than 20,000 self-declaration forms from individuals seeking nomination as candidates during election years.
The commission has also investigated 228 allegations involving forged academic and professional certificates, recommending prosecution in 134 files forwarded to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions.
Of those cases, 60 are pending before courts, while 50 have been concluded, resulting in 45 convictions and five acquittals.
EACC has also recovered Sh41.2 million acquired through the use of forged academic and professional qualifications.
Mohamud said the commission would continue examining documents submitted alongside self-declaration forms to prevent falsified certificates from being used to secure clearance for elective positions.

items.summary:

Ruto said the company, which was on the b
items.text:
BUNGOMA, Kenya, Nov 23 – President William Ruto has hailed the leasing of Nzoia Sugar Company to private investor Rai Group, describing the miller’s turnaround as historic following improvements in production, profitability and payments to sugarcane farmers.
Ruto said the company, which was on the brink of collapse three years ago, had undergone significant operational changes under private management, crediting Rai Group with introducing professionalism and efficiency.
Speaking at Nzoia Sugar Company grounds in Kanduyi Constituency, Bungoma County, on Monday, the President issued bonus cheques worth Sh195 million to farmers supplying sugarcane to the factory.
The payment forms part of Sh1.2 billion being distributed to farmers across the Western sugar belt.
“Four years ago, when we stood on these very grounds and pledged to revive this factory, it was one of the most inefficient facilities in this part of the world,” Ruto said.
He noted that farmers were now receiving payments for cane deliveries within a week, while factory employees were earning their salaries on time.
“Today, farmers are paid for cane deliveries within a week while workers receive their salaries on time at the end of every month. This is a historic day for Nzoia Sugar Company,” he said.
The President added that the miller was now paying taxes to the Government and contributing to economic growth.
Nzoia Sugar Company Managing Director Tejveer Rai disclosed that the company had paid Sh1.6 billion to sugarcane farmers this year, alongside Sh150 million to cane harvesters.
He said the miller had also remitted Sh688 million in taxes to the National Government and Bungoma County, in addition to Sh639 million in lease and concession fees.
Rai further revealed that the company was investing Sh5.7 billion in factory modernisation, with some of the new equipment already in transit.
The President maintained that Nzoia Sugar Company remained the property of the people of Bungoma, dismissing claims by opposition leaders that the Government had surrendered ownership of the facility through the leasing arrangement.
“We have an agreement with the operators of this facility. The factory and the nucleus estate will continue to be the property of the people of Bungoma,” he said.
Ruto cautioned politicians against using the company’s previous challenges for political expediency, arguing that the ongoing transformation demonstrated the Government’s commitment to reviving the sugar industry.
“Wake up and smell the coffee. Nzoia has changed for the better, forever,” he said.
He maintained that his administration had fulfilled its commitment to restore the factory, recalling the promise he made to farmers at the same venue.
The President also pledged to double bonus payments to Nzoia farmers next year as the company’s performance and profitability improve.
Ruto announced that he would issue bonus cheques to farmers supplying Mumias Sugar Company next week, with similar payments planned for farmers supplying Chemelil, Muhoroni, Miwani and Sony sugar factories.
He observed that sugarcane farming had previously become unprofitable for many farmers, who would deliver their produce only to be informed that they owed money to the millers.
The President said the sector had significant room for expansion, noting that national sugar production stood at 790,000 metric tonnes last year.
He projected production would rise to 900,000 metric tonnes this year, putting the country on course to achieve the target of 1.2 million metric tonnes required to attain sugar self-sufficiency.
Ruto said growth in the agricultural sector was translating into improved earnings and better livelihoods for farmers.
“Our competitors who are trying to lie to Kenyans that we are doing nothing, we are waiting for you with a track record of performance and delivery,” he said.
On infrastructure, the President announced that the Government would soon begin dualling the Malaba-Kimaeti section of the Eldoret-Malaba Highway at a cost of Sh3 billion.
He said the project would complement ongoing construction of the Rironi-Mau Summit Highway, with the two road projects expected to meet in the middle.
“As work on the Rironi-Mau Summit Highway continues, we will begin here so that the two projects meet in the middle,” he said.
Those present included National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula, Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi, Cooperatives Cabinet Secretary Wycliffe Oparanya, Bungoma Governor Ken Lusaka, Members of Parliament and other leaders.

items.text:
Atletico's Simeone breaks La Liga victories record
- Published
Atletico Madrid's 3-0 victory over Getafe may have been routine, but the win was another landmark in manager Diego Simeone's lengthy tenure at the club.
Sunday's triumph at Estadio Coliseum was the Argentine's 345th La Liga win in his 567th match, surpassing the record for the most victories in the Spanish top flight.
Simeone beat the mark of legendary former Atletico and Spain manager Luis Aragones, who won 344 matches but needed 189 more games to reach that total.
"It makes me happy," Simeone said of setting the new mark, with his side now third in the table after 10 wins from 13 games.
"I don't usually find many things to be happy about, but there is an incredible amount of work behind this."
Questioned about the perception that his team are defensive, Simeone said that was a "constant criticism we face".
He added: "I don't place much value on it, but I do take note of it.
"This narrative that we're a defensive team, as if we're always playing solely to defend. You don't win 345 matches just by defending. Is that even possible?"
The 56-year-old has been in charge of Atletico since December 2011, joining the club in an era when Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid and Pep Guardiola's Barcelona were the dominant teams in Spain.
He outlasted the pair of managerial superstars, leading Atletico into a period of consistent success and staying with his side long enough to witness Mourinho's return to Real this summer, 13 years after his initial departure.
Having won the Europa League in May 2012, after his appointment on 23 December 2011, Simeone led Atletico to the European Super Cup title three months later.
He then won the Copa del Rey in his first full season and secured the club's first La Liga title since 1996 - when Simeone was an Atletico player - in the following campaign.
Atletico have established themselves as the third force in Spanish football under his leadership, qualifying for the Champions League in every full season under his charge.
However he has been unable to win European football's premier competition, losing in the final to city rivals Real twice in heart-breaking fashion - in extra-time in 2014 after Real scored a stoppage-time equaliser, and on penalties in 2016.
Simeone's last silverware arrived in 2021 when he won a second Spanish league championship, while he also guided the team to a Europa League and Super Cup double in 2018.
His contract expires at the end of this season with the Atletico fanbase now waiting to see if their manager intends to extend his remarkable victory record into another campaign.

items.title: EACC targets youth in national campaign to promote ethical leadership ahead of 2027 polls
items.summary:
NAIROBI,Kenya, Nov 23 – The Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) will roll out a national integrity awareness campaign targeting voters, with a special focus on young people, ahead of the August 2027 General Election.
The campaign will seek to educate Kenyans on the constitutional and ethica
items.text:
NAIROBI,Kenya, Nov 23 – The Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) will roll out a national integrity awareness campaign targeting voters, with a special focus on young people, ahead of the August 2027 General Election.
The campaign will seek to educate Kenyans on the constitutional and ethical standards expected of individuals seeking elective positions while promoting responsible citizenship, peaceful electoral participation and informed voting.
EACC Commissioner Col. (Rtd) Alfred Mshimba said the initiative was part of efforts to address the country’s persistent leadership integrity challenges by empowering voters to scrutinise candidates before entrusting them with public office.
He said enforcement alone would not deliver ethical leadership, calling for greater public participation in demanding accountability from political leaders.
“Our message is simple: Do not just prepare to vote. Prepare to vote wisely. Do not just prepare to participate. Prepare to participate responsibly,” Mshimba said.
He was speaking during a workshop for media practitioners on integrity in leadership and elections at Whitesands Beach Resort in Mombasa.
Mshimba said the campaign would particularly target young people, whose role in shaping the country’s political future had become increasingly significant.
He cited the youth-led protests of 2024 and 2025 as evidence of growing public demand for accountable leadership, noting that corruption, high taxation and the accumulation of wealth by public officials had featured prominently among the grievances.
However, he warned against attempts by politicians to exploit young people’s political awareness by recruiting them to intimidate opponents, disrupt public gatherings and perpetrate electoral violence.
“Do not allow anyone to use you as a weapon today and abandon you tomorrow. When violence breaks out, it is often the young people who are injured, arrested or lose their lives,” he cautioned.
The Commission said it would work with the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), the National Cohesion and Integration Commission and other investigative agencies to address electoral corruption, violence and other integrity violations.
In a separate address delivered on his behalf by EACC Director of Investigations Paschal Mweu, Chief Executive Officer Abdi Mohamud said the Commission would also establish public reporting desks during the awareness campaign to receive complaints on corruption and ethical violations.
The desks will provide an avenue for members of the public to report voter bribery, public officers engaging in partisan political campaigns and other violations ahead of the elections.
Mohamud said the Commission was already aware of allegations of voter bribery during recent by-elections and pledged to investigate the claims, gather evidence and prosecute those found culpable.
He also urged public officers to refrain from engaging in political campaigns in violation of the Conflict of Interest Act, warning that those found culpable would face legal action.
The CEO further clarified that EACC’s mandate in elections is to investigate integrity concerns and submit recommendations on the suitability of candidates to the IEBC, rather than directly barring individuals from contesting.
The Commission receives more than 20,000 self-declaration forms from individuals seeking nomination as candidates during election years.
Mshimba challenged the media to support the awareness drive by giving prominence to integrity issues, scrutinising the records of those seeking public office and amplifying the voices of young people advocating for peaceful and accountable leadership.

items.title: CoG Tells County Hospitals to Ignore PS Oluga’s Directive on SHA Paybill Numbers
items.summary: NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 23 – The Council of Governors (CoG) has directed managers of county health facilities to disregard a directive by Medical Services Principal Secretary Ouma Oluga ordering the removal of Paybill numbers from public hospitals, escalating a dispute over the management of healthcare s
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 23 – The Council of Governors (CoG) has directed managers of county health facilities to disregard a directive by Medical Services Principal Secretary Ouma Oluga ordering the removal of Paybill numbers from public hospitals, escalating a dispute over the management of healthcare services under devolution.
Speaking durng a press conference on Monday, the Council’s Chairperson Muthomi Njuki termed Oluga’s directive unconstitutional, arguing that it undermines county governments’ authority to manage health facilities and threatens lawful cost-recovery mechanisms.
Oluga had directed Social Health Authority (SHA) compliance officers to remove Paybill numbers from county health facilities nationwide, arguing that Kenyans are covered under the national health insurance framework.
However, Njuki maintains that county governments have constitutional and statutory responsibility for managing county health facilities, overseeing service delivery and determining applicable fees and charges.
“The Ministry of Health Principal Secretary has no supervisory authority over county entities, their accounting officers, County Assemblies or governors,” he stated.
He nevertheless agreed with the Health Cabinet Secretary that patients should not be required to make out-of-pocket payments for services already covered and fully reimbursed by SHA.
He, however, cautioned against assuming that registration with SHA automatically guarantees access to every healthcare service or that all Kenyans are fully covered.
“SHA operates under defined benefit packages, tariffs, eligibility requirements and coverage limits, meaning some medical services may fall outside the scheme,” he said.
He cited excluded services, exhausted benefits, co-payments, rejected claims and specialised treatments as areas that may require alternative lawful payment arrangements.
He also raised concerns over delayed or unpaid SHA claims and operational challenges affecting public health facilities.
“New electronic contracting requirements could further complicate the participation of public hospitals in the scheme, potentially limiting access to specialised services, including cancer treatment.”
According to the Council, removing Paybill numbers without addressing these gaps could disrupt hospital operations and undermine the ability of facilities to recover costs for services not covered by SHA.
The COG Chairpeson called on Oluga to avoid making “sweeping public declarations on matters affecting county health facilities and instead engage county governments through established consultation and intergovernmental cooperation frameworks.”
He maintained that the implementation of Universal Health Coverage must respect the constitutional distribution of functions between the national and county governments.
The dispute comes amid the government’s ongoing transition to the SHA framework, which is intended to expand access to healthcare and reduce the financial burden on patients.
The governors insist that efforts to eliminate double payments must be balanced against the need to ensure that county hospitals have lawful mechanisms to meet costs for services and treatments not covered by the national scheme.

Harrison Armstrong's distance covered stats highlight Everton midfielder's impact under David Moyes this season
In this exclusive interview with David Moyes, the Everton manager discusses the development of Harrison Armstrong since being recalled from a loan spell at Preston North End and the reasons why he believes the 19-year-old midfielder can still improve...
Monday 23 November 2026 10:07, UK
Harrison Armstrong has started every Premier League game for Everton this season, ranking in the top three for distance covered in the competition going into the weekend. This has been some year for a player who started 2026 on loan at Preston North End.
There was talk of a big move to Nottingham Forest in the summer and interest from elsewhere remains as Everton try to persuade him to sign a new contract. Supporters will be desperate for one of their own to stay. And David Moyes feel the same way.
"He is a big player for us," the Everton manager tells Sky Sports. "For a 19-year-old young midfield player he is doing really well. I hope he can continue to do that." That recall from Preston in January already feels like a pivotal moment in Armstrong's career.

- No Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract📺
"I was watching him quite regularly. He was doing really well and we had to bring him back. They did not like it obviously because Preston were going really well. But we had got so many injuries around December time that we needed to bring him back."
In truth, it was not ideal for Armstrong in some respects. "I think if he had got another 20 games with them it would have been good for him." But there were opportunities off the bench and the fact that he did not have things all his own way will have helped him too.
There were substitute appearances against Arsenal and Manchester City when he was brought on to help tighten things up only for Everton to concede late. But even those experiences are useful. "He is a confident boy. He has got a lot of belief in himself."
Most importantly, he has responded. "Since then he has stepped up again." Speaking to Moyes at Everton's training ground, he acknowledges that it was Armstrong's work in the summer that made him sit up and take notice. "He was very good in pre-season."
Moyes explains: "There was no way we could really put him back out on loan this year. We knew that we would find more minutes for him. But his form in pre-season games was the reason which made me think that we were certainly centred around him."
Circumstances helped. "We lost Jimmy Garner with a hernia operation in the opening games of the season, which left Hayden Hackney, who had just arrived and was still carrying a bit of an injury from last season. So it gave Harrison the opportunity to start."
In Moyes' words, it was a chance "to show what he could do" and Armstrong has done just that. "He has taken it with both hands." The youngster's obvious enthusiasm instantly endeared him to an Everton crowd that demand work rate from their players.
Those distance-covered statistics stand out but Armstrong sets the tone for Everton with his off-the-ball work. "You have got to have some attributes which are really important and that one is really important for him and for us," Moyes explains.
"He works incredibly hard for the team."
The result is that even with Garner and Hackney fit, he has stayed in. "Without doubt he has earned the right to be in the team. He has earned the right by his performances every week because we have got competition. But if you are doing as well as he is…"
Of course, Moyes remains the archetypal tough-taskmaster and it is only natural that the 63-year-old Scot opts to couch his praise for the player with a reminder that Armstrong must add more to his game if he is to fulfil his potential in the long term.
"There are things we want him to improve on. He has still got a bit to learn." What exactly? "We would like him to do a bit better with his passing at times and I certainly want him to score more goals or get more opportunities. They would be the things."
But there is optimism that he can add these elements. "We must not forget that he is a 19-year-old midfield player and very much learning his trade." Moyes knows. He has overseen the development of top-class teenagers from Wayne Rooney to Declan Rice.
What is his verdict on how good Armstrong could go on to become? "I think that he can develop into a really top-notch midfield player," adds Moyes. It has been a breakout year for him in the Premier League. But this could be just the start for Harrison Armstrong.

items.title: 'Price knows he can win Worlds after Grand Slam glory'

Gerwyn Price: Wayne Mardle says Welshman knows he can win World Championship again after fourth Grand Slam title

items.text:
Gerwyn Price: Wayne Mardle says Welshman knows he can win World Championship again after fourth Grand Slam title
Is Gerwyn Price the favourite to win his second world title at Alexandra Palace after beating Gian van Veen in the Grand Slam of Darts final?; you can watch the World Darts Championship live on Sky Sports from December 11
Sunday 22 November 2026 23:10, UK
Wayne Mardle says Gerwyn Price knows he can win the World Championship at Alexandra Palace again after ending his major trophy drought to claim a fourth Grand Slam title.
'The Iceman' had not won a major televised event since 2022 and may have thought it might not happen again after losing three finals this year alone.
But with Luke Littler and Luke Humphries exiting early, Price took his chance with a brilliant 16-11 win over Gian van Veen in Wolverhampton.
- Darts in 2026: Key dates, calendar, results 📅
- Got Sky? Watch on the Sky Sports app 📱
- Not got Sky? Get instant access with NOW 📺
Price claimed Grand Slam glory for the first time since 2021 - the same year he won his sole world title, when he was forced to celebrate behind closed doors due to the Covid-19 pandemic.
"Gezzy knows he can win it. Yes, winning the Grand Slam four times is amazing for him, but he knows he can win the Worlds," said Mardle.
"He's done it before and he's got a new-found fanbase.
"He's enjoying himself and it's incredible the way that everything's turned around for him. And, look, he's enjoying life.
"It's good to see Gezzy smile."
Looking ahead to Ally Pally, 'Hawaii 501' said: "Those that are at the top of the tree right now, call it top six, top five, top four, they're the ones to beat. They really are.
"Luke Humphries, Luke Littler, Gezzy Price.
"Let's be honest, we know that he got beat [in the semi-finals] and didn't play great but Michael van Gerwen shone this week.
"Don't rule out a fourth world title for him. With timing and a bit of luck, anyone can win."
'Price is talking about the next one already'
Mark Webster said it does not look like Price is done after returning to the winners' circle with his eighth major title.
Price will be eyeing further televised success at the Players Championship Finals which takes place at Butlin's Minehead Resort from November 27-29.
Van Veen, Humphries and Van Gerwen will also headline, as a 64-player field compete in the final tournament before the 2027 World Darts Championship.
"He's still got tournaments to win. He's talking about the next one already," said Webster.
"He goes to Minehead and he's talking about this trend with winning this and winning the Worlds.
"He wants another World Championship, and particularly all the heartache he's had getting to finals this year, to get over the line, really important for him. It could open up some floodgates for him now to go on and win major after major."
The 2008 Lakeside world champion believes the cream will rise to the top on the grandest stage of them all.
"At the Worlds, there'll be upsets, but I think it will come to the top players," said Webster as Price aims to follow Michael Smith, Humphries and Littler - twice over the past four years - to win the Slam and then go on to win the Worlds in just over a month.
"I think the two Lukes left this event - they just got beat by the better player. There's no real concern in the way they played, so they'll be a force, along with Price, Gian, and it's good to see Michael [Van Gerwen] in glimpses, but it's going to be a brilliant three weeks at Ally Pally."
Has winning the Grand Slam done Price a huge favour?
Victory for Price means he is provisionally up to world No 3, with Littler still No 1, Van Veen at No 2, and Humphries down to No 4 - potentially shaking up the draw heading into the Worlds.
Price, who took home the £200,000 jackpot in Wolverhampton, has also overtaken Littler with the most ranking money earned this season.
Commentator Dan Dawson explained: "Price has had to battle to this title, and I think he's had to battle to win this Grand Slam more than he has in any other since his first, because we've seen him play unbelievable stuff to win Grand Slam titles.
"But I think that's what he's had to do to become a winner again, and seeing him smile and seeing that pressure lift, just hearing him talk, I think that is an enormous sign because he's already looking ahead. What can I win next?
"We know that at Ally Pally he is up into No 3 in the world, with Humphries and Littler on the same side of the draw provisionally.
"That game there between Gian and Price, that would provisionally be the semi-final in the other half of the draw.
"So that has done him a favour if he is looking to become a world champion again."

items.title: Fury reveals schizophrenia diagnosis
items.summary:
Tyson Fury reveals schizophrenia and bipolar disorder diagnosis ahead of Anthony Joshua fight
Tyson Fury has opened up on being diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder in a new feature-length Netflix documentary; Fury was diagnosed following his victory against Wladimir Klitschko in 2015;
items.text:
Tyson Fury reveals schizophrenia and bipolar disorder diagnosis ahead of Anthony Joshua fight
Tyson Fury has opened up on being diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder in a new feature-length Netflix documentary; Fury was diagnosed following his victory against Wladimir Klitschko in 2015; he is preparing to fight Anthony Joshua on December 11
Monday 23 November 2026 11:54, UK
Tyson Fury has opened up about being diagnosed with schizophrenia following his ascent to becoming world heavyweight champion in 2015.
Fury is set to end his long wait to fight Anthony Joshua on December 11, and ahead of the blockbuster British bout, a new feature-length Netflix documentary, TYSON FURY, will shed light on his career and his mental health struggles.
Fury defeated Wladimir Klitschko in November 2015, and was due to fight the Ukrainian again in October 2016, but withdrew after being declared "medically unfit to fight".
- Harrison: Fury and Joshua have a genuine animosity
- Joshua unable to see new daughter until after Fury fight
- Read the latest, news, updates and video ahead of Fury vs AJ
After his victory against Klitschko, the 'Gypsy King' revealed he had struggled with drug and alcohol addiction and had gained weight.
He was admitted to hospital in June 2016 with a suspected heart attack, and revealed that while in hospital he had heard voices in his head.
"Words can't explain the darkness I was in," Fury said during the Netflix documentary, which is due to air on November 27.
"It was like a living version of the pits of hell.
"I thought I would end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.
"The anxiety was crippling me. I just could not overcome it and that's when I went and saw the psychiatrist down in London. She asked me a gazillion questions, and I ticked all the boxes. Depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder."
During his stay in hospital, Fury explained he believed the "radio started talking to me" and voices had threatened to kill him and his family.
His wife Paris, whom he married in 2008, visited her husband in hospital and was told by doctors that the British fighter had suffered an anxiety attack.
"I was so scared, scared for him. I could see he was gone, he'd flipped the switch," Paris said.
Paris added: "[The doctors said] he's a mild schizophrenic and even then, the penny didn't drop.
"I was like: 'Don't be silly, what's she on about schizophrenic? Maniacs are schizophrenic, you're not schizophrenic'.
"I'd never heard of bipolar. When someone actually explained it to me, it was: 'Wow, that's him to a T'."
The NHS says Schizophrenia is a long-term mental health illness that is a form of psychosis.
Those suffering from the condition may, at times, be unable to distinguish their own thoughts from reality. Symptoms can include hallucinations and delusions.
The NHS describes bipolar disorder as a mental health issue where a person can experience extreme changes in their mood.
Fury, who has been open about his struggles with mental health in the past, spoke during the documentary about how he would go on to seek professional help for his condition.
He would return to professional boxing three years after his victory over Klitschko, before winning the WBC world heavyweight belt with a victory over Deontay Wilder in December 2018.
During the documentary, Fury credits his family for helping him through that period.
"If you look at my life, there's a lot of achievements, a lot of good stuff, a lot of success," he said.
"But the most successful thing I have in my life is my family, my kids and my wife."

If you are worried about your mental health, get advice and support through your GP or call the NHS on 111.

Liverpool showed their attacking power with a 4-0 victory over rivals Man Utd; the visitors at Anfield had Leny Yoro sent off early on and Florian Wirtz pulled them apart; the German is f
items.text:
Liverpool's attack shows its devastating potential as Florian Wirtz steps up in thumping win over 10-man Man Utd
Liverpool showed their attacking power with a 4-0 victory over rivals Man Utd; the visitors at Anfield had Leny Yoro sent off early on and Florian Wirtz pulled them apart; the German is finally showing his quality in the Premier League as Andoni Iraola's attack begins to click
Monday 23 November 2026 09:44, UK
The conditions were favourable. Leny Yoro's red card after just eight minutes. A Man Utd team devoid of confidence and defensive resilience. But on Sunday, Liverpool's attack showed its devastating potential.
"We've questioned the attacking players but they looked absolutely electric," purred Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher after his former side had put four past their biggest rivals.
Carragher has been clear in his criticism of Liverpool's expensively-assembled frontline previously. In August, he suggested Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz - brought in for £240m - were part of a summer 2025 splurge which could go down as the "arguably the worst transfer window we've probably seen in Premier League history".
Under new boss Andoni Iraola, those Liverpool players are starting to shift the narrative now.
"The attacking players from Liverpool certainly turned up today," agreed Sky Sports' Roy Keane, amid his dressing down of United's defending.
Key to Liverpool's attacking play was the much-maligned Wirtz.
- Liverpool 4-0 Man Utd - Match report and reaction
- Liverpool scores and fixtures | FREE PL highlights▶️
- Want to watch Liverpool games? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract
According to Opta, he created five big chances in the game. That's the most by a player in their records for that metric, dating back to 2010.
For context, Wirtz had created just one big chance in his previous 10 Premier League games this term - that came in his last outing at Crystal Palace, where he also scored his first goal of the season. His next came at Anfield, brilliantly flicking in a quickfire second for his side after Dominik Szoboszlai's free-kick to give 10-man United little hope of a result.
It's been a long wait but it seems to finally be coming together in England for the undoubtedly talented 23-year-old. "This is why they spent the money on him," said Carragher.
Wirtz's own assessment of his form gave a nod to his team-mates. "I feel very good, but I think it's also because the team has just developed and gets better," he said. "Being part of this, you also get better. I'm enjoying this."
The development, though, runs beyond just a set group of starting attackers. It's the options and variety at Iraola's disposal which can make Liverpool fans optimistic.
Alexander Isak leads the line but, without Cody Gakpo in the side on Sunday, there was the chance for 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha to step up and he seized it, assisting Wirtz and then converting Bradley Barcola's cross to become the youngest scorer against United in Premier League history.
Ngumoha's expected assists total for the game of 1.05 was the second highest by a player in a Premier League game this season. Top spot was taken by Wirtz, with 1.08.
Victor Munoz then stepped off the bench to add a fourth from a Wirtz pass - the third time the German has teed up Munoz in a Premier League game this season.
And there is still Hugo Ekitike to come back from his injury.
Liverpool are still developing and it wasn't always perfect at Anfield. They missed six big chances to further punish United, while Isak went goalless from an xG of 1.32. Barcola, too, was at times erratic, completing just one of his seven dribbles.
The quality of their opposition shouldn't be lost, either. Liverpool are the third team to put four past United in the past month.
Iraola, though, called on his side to deliver a statement Premier League win at Anfield for the first time this season before the match and his players delivered.
The challenge is to realise that attacking potential consistently in the tests to come. But with Wirtz finally starting to shine, Liverpool's future looks bright.

items.text:
Kenya and DR Congo agree to restore ties after tensions over conflict
- Published
Kenya's President William Ruto and his Congolese counterpart Felix Tshisekedi have agreed to restore full diplomatic ties between the two countries following tensions over the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
Relations between the two countries have soured since 2023 when DR Congo accused Kenya of hosting leaders launching a rebel alliance, including the M23.
This led DR Congo to recall its envoy to Nairobi. Relations deteriorated further when Kinshasa refusing to accredit Kenya's nominated ambassador.
On Sunday, the two leaders affirmed their commitment to "sovereignty, territorial integrity, non-interference in the internal affairs of states".
The agreement was announced in a joint statement issued after the summit held in the town of Oyo in Congo-Brazzaville, facilitated by the nation's President Denis Sassou Nguesso, with Togolese leader Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé as mediator.
Tshisekedi and Ruto also agreed to "good neighbourliness and peaceful settlement of disputes" as well as "strengthen cooperation within regional mechanisms".
DR Congo and Kenya are both members of the East African Community (EAC).
DR Congo, which joined in 2022, is the latest entrant to the bloc, but its membership has been complicated by its accusation that Rwanda, a fellow member, backs the M23 rebels. Rwanda denies the claims despite overwhelming evidence.
DR Congo has also accused Kenya of hosting Congolese political and rebel leaders whom it says are working to destabilise the country.
When the Congo River Alliance (AFC), a political-military alliance including the M23, was launched in Nairobi in 2023, DR Congo responded by recalling its ambassador to Kenya.
The tensions were stoked further in March last year after Kenya named a consul-general to Goma, the capital of DR Congo's North Kivu region, after it fell to M23 forces, who control many eastern parts of the country.
DR Congo said naming the envoy amounted to disrespect for the country's territorial integrity and seemed to legitimise the group's occupation.
- Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader 
  - Published31 October
Relations deteriorated further after Kenya hosted a meeting of Congolese opposition figures, including former President Joseph Kabila, in October 2025.
Kabila was in 2025 sentenced to death in absentia on charges including war crimes and treason. He denied the accusations, but did not appear in court to defend himself.
He has since been named the leader of the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), the new rebel coalition that took over from the AFC.
Sunday's meeting between Ruto and Tshisekedi also included other issues including deepening trade cooperation, economic development, and regional integration.
The two also sought to collaborate to control the spread of the Ebola virus.
On Sunday, the head of the World Health Organization (WHO), Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, said the frequency of attacks across the country's east had increased since the end of October, seriously affecting the Ebola response.
Tedros said heavy fighting in an area close to where the Ebola outbreak first emerged had disrupted work and the wider Ebola response.
More than 5,700 people have died and 11,000 infected with Ebola in DR Congo since the outbreak was declared in May.
The latest outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo species of the virus, has spread beyond DR Congo borders, with cases reported in Kenya, Uganda and Nigeria.

items.text:
Holloway sacked by Swindon after two seasons
- Published
Manager Ian Holloway has been sacked by Swindon Town after just over two years in charge.
The Robins' 2-0 loss at Newport County on Saturday left them 17th in League Two and was their fourth successive loss in all competitions - conceding 10 goals in the process.
They have won just two of their last 15 matches going back to the start of September and, at the beginning of October, Holloway described himself as a "dead man walking" if the team's form did not turn around.
- Swindon's Holloway labels himself dead man walking 
  - Published2 October
Holloway was appointed in October 2024 initially on a deal until the end of that season, with the club at the time a place off the relegation zone.
He surpassed 1,000 games managing in English football two months later and went on to sign a new two-year deal in March 2025, having steered Swindon clear of the drop and into play-off contention form.
Promotion was the aim last season with Holloway issuing a rallying call at the start of the campaign for Swindon to be the "team I believe we can" be.
Things started well, with the Robins in the top five of the table from August 2025 and in the automatic promotion spots in February, but a run of three wins in their final 13 games saw them fall to seventh and they lost 2-1 to Chesterfield in a must-win final match of the campaign to miss the play-offs.
The slump in form has continued as the 2026-27 season started, and while they did win three of their first five league games, they are winless in their past five (four losses, one draw), scoring just one goal in that time.

items.title: ‘Haaland must be worried’: Thierno Barry’s rise has David Moyes purring
items.summary: A most unexpected name sits behind the phenomenon Erling Haaland and the £125m proven marksman Alexander Isak in the Premier League goalscoring chart this season. The rise of Thierno Barry may have surprised even the man himself but stands as a fitting reward for single-minded perseverance and the r
items.text:
A most unexpected name sits behind the phenomenon Erling Haaland and the £125m proven marksman Alexander Isak in the Premier League goalscoring chart this season. The rise of Thierno Barry may have surprised even the man himself but stands as a fitting reward for single-minded perseverance and the refusal to quit.
“Fabulous” was David Moyes’s take on Barry’s last performance for Everton, when a double against Coventry took the striker to 10 goals for the season in all competitions and his team temporarily up to fifth. It was high praise indeed from a manager who does not dispense tributes freely, and can appear to be on the French forward’s case constantly, but was no more than Barry deserved for a display that also featured an assist for Everton’s third goal of the night. His six Premier League goals leave him joint third alongside Evanilson of Bournemouth and Aston Villa’s Nicolas Jackson.
“Haaland must be worried about him catching him now,” Moyes said. That line was delivered in jest but also represented a welcome departure from the position Barry found himself in this summer, and from where Everton stood at the close of transfer deadline day.
“I’m stopping, I’m stopping,” says Barry in a searingly honest video released on his YouTube channel in September. Entitled Never Give Up, the episode shows the striker doing exactly that after one miss too many during a private training session with his personal coach. He then breaks down in tears, head in hands in despair, after a dressing down from his lawyer. “Don’t give up, bro,” snaps the lawyer. “Where you come from, you can’t give up.”
Many players in that position would have buried the footage, afraid of broadcasting weakness or of the vicious comments that would invariably follow on social media. Barry told the BBC he spent three weeks worrying whether to post before deciding: “No, I just need to show myself. They need to learn about me because last season I showed a version of me that is not me. And they need to learn about me, how I train hard to be the best on the pitch.”
Barry’s openness was refreshingly well received, even online. In the episode he admits hitting “rock bottom several times last season” when, after a £27m move from Villarreal, he went 16 games without a goal for Everton and failed to register a shot on target until December. He finished his debut campaign in English football with eight goals from 41 appearances, a tally surpassed in 13 matches this season, and was often watching Beto from the bench.
Never Give Up is revealing not only for Barry’s emotional side. It features the striker having private training sessions in England, France and Morocco in the summer. The personal coach, lawyer and personal physio who make an appearance are part of an entourage that also includes a nutritionist and a chef. Barry will not be found wanting in his efforts to establish himself in the Premier League, a process well under way before Everton’s visit to Brentford on Monday night.
“His general all-round play has improved,” says Moyes. “There’s lots of his all-round play that still needs to get better but I’d say his game knowledge, his understanding, has improved. I would never do down any leagues but I think coming to the Premier League from abroad is really difficult in the first year. I think he found it difficult. The expectation on players coming in and being good immediately is built up and he’s needed time to settle.
“He still needs lots of things to make him a rounded centre-forward but there are bits of it that are getting better; he’s beginning to look more clinical. Even in training I’m seeing much better actions than I did last year. Leighton Baines does quite a lot with him, and shows him stuff to make him better, but his integration is much better now too.”
Barry can be a bewildering player capable of inexplicable misses and touches one minute, clinical finishes and creative distribution the next. Everton’s only recognised forward should be closer to Haaland’s tally of 14 club goals for the season. But it is only five years since he started playing as a striker for Sochaux, who he joined after failing in trials as a defender for Clermont and as a central midfielder with Hamilton Academical. Lyon-born, Barry did not come through the academy system in France that could have polished the rough edges. He has had to do it all for himself and, fortunately for Everton given their calamitous end to the transfer window, he has stepped up at the right time.
Moyes, far from just being on Barry’s case, believes the 24-year-old’s story can inspire others. “It should definitely be factored in,” he says of how people should judge a player without an academy background. “Also, not understanding how it works at football clubs and how you go about it. Not in terms of how you behave – he is not a problem in that department – but just how you go about your job and what is expected of you. He is still getting used to it.
“He was in France, then went to Basel [via Beveren in Belgium], then Basel to Villarreal and then Villarreal to here. He also had quite a lot of rejections before he even got out of France, by all accounts. But there is also inspiration behind that. You can show young people that if you put the work in, keep challenging yourself and keep pushing yourself, somebody might just like what they see and pick you up.
“Basel saw something in him and obviously other clubs have decided to go for it as well. We took him as a young, inexperienced centre-forward for £27m, and a year and a half ago it was probably a worse time to be looking for strikers in the market. What ones who were bought at that time have done absolutely brilliantly? Not many. We took a gamble early. Has the gamble paid off? It’s beginning to look better than maybe it did last year but that is because of Thierno’s hard work.”

The gl
items.text:
What to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. If not, United are heading only one way: down. Jamie Jackson
Liverpool in late 2026 feature three £100m-plus signings. Each of them enjoyed among their best moments yet at Anfield. Florian Wirtz appeared refreshed by working over the international break with Jürgen Klopp, clearly still a scouse whisperer. Wirtz scored an improvised goal and set up another among 10 chances he created. Alexander Isak exposing Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro for the latter’s dismissal was the moment to break the dam. If Bradley Barcola showed that finishing might not be his forte, his assist for Rio Ngumoha’s goal evidenced there is composure to accompany lightning speed. Ngumoha showed he has the talent to fetch a similar price tag, scoring and assisting at 18 years and 85 days, the youngest Liverpool player to do so since Michael Owen versus Leeds in December 1997. If Manchester United’s performance, and Mauricio Pochettino’s bizarre selection of De Ligt, opened the door, Liverpool stormed through it. Beating United never gets old, no matter their desiccated state. John Brewin
It has been a long time between drinks for Hull when it comes to Premier League wins: three months, in fact. Perhaps that is why the celebrations were so extreme after their win over Brighton on Sunday – though the manner of it, two injury-time goals after absorbing so much pressure all afternoon, will have contributed too. It was a much-needed victory for Hull, who continue to show signs they are perhaps the best equipped of the three promoted teams to survive. The gap to the relegation zome is now five points and their win underlined why the Tigers have the two real ingredients needed to survive. Konstantinos Tzolakis produced the goalkeeping display of the Premier League season to deny Brighton time and time again, while Oli McBurnie’s late double exemplified the kind of goal-poaching Hull will need if they are to beat the drop. Keep those two areas thriving, and Hull can perhaps look upwards, rather than over their shoulders. Aaron Bower
When Yasir al-Rumayyan, over from Riyadh to watch Matthias Jaissle’s team live for the first time this season, studied his team sheet, Newcastle’s chair presumably read between the lines. There was no space for Bazoumana Touré or Aladji Bamba (who cost a combined £78.5m) on a substitutes’ bench that in Nico González and Matias Fernandez-Pardo featured more than £100m worth of summer signings. Meanwhile, Amar Dedic and Sean Steur (a joint £50m outlay) were withdrawn at half-time and replaced by two members of Newcastle’s old guard, Tino Livramento and Jacob Ramsey. They played key roles in a renascent second half performance, with Jaissle’s revitalised team overcoming a 1-0 deficit to draw 2-2 against table-topping Arsenal. Afterwards Jaissle and al-Rumayyan chatted. “The chair analysed the game the way I did,” he said. “He knows about football.” Newcastle’s manager wants an increased say in a recruitment process currently controlled by sporting director Ross Wilson. Significantly, the goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek was the sole summer buy to feature in the second half. Over to you, Yasir. Louise Taylor
Chelsea’s injury list was no excuse for their performance in their 4-1 defeat by Leeds. They have spent more than £1bn putting this squad together and still had an £117m attacking midfielder, Morgan Rogers, in the starting XI. Leeds, by contrast, have had to be smarter with their budget and Daniel Farke has revitalised players who previously looked unlikely to flourish in the Premier League. Ethan Ampadu had to drop down a level after leaving Chelsea, while Jayden Bogle was relegated with Sheffield United five years ago. James Justin suffered a serious achilles injury not long after making his England debut in 2022 and Dominic Calvert-Lewin was close to being written off after leaving Everton in 2025. Yet Farke has found ways to improve these players. They are not fashionable names and did not cost much, but they are being coached well and are in a team with an identity. There is none of that at Chelsea. Jacob Steinberg
Enzo Maresca is still in the experimentation stage as Manchester City manager. Maybe the seven straight Premier League wins to start was a false indication of where the team are, in terms of progression in the post-Pep Guardiola era. It’s inevitable that a team will dip once the early adrenaline wears off and Maresca is finding this out. To rectify his team’s slow play and lack of energy, the all-action Elliot Anderson was pushed further forward to provide the thrust from the middle of the park, while his teammates were pedestrian. Ayyoub Bouaddi was given the responsibility of sitting, with Enzo Fernández left out. “We are trying to find different solutions, right balance, and to be more consistent,” Maresca said. It looks difficult to fit all three into the team and Maresca is yet to find the right answer after four games without a win, leaving the manager to return to the lab. Will Unwin

items.summary:
Max Verstappen rivalry with George Russell 'a good factor' of F1 entertainment, says Mercedes chief Toto Wolff
A long-standing feud between Max Verstappen and George Russell was reignited at the Las Vegas Grand Prix; Russell criticised Verstappen following a collision between the pair in final pract
items.text:
Max Verstappen rivalry with George Russell 'a good factor' of F1 entertainment, says Mercedes chief Toto Wolff
A long-standing feud between Max Verstappen and George Russell was reignited at the Las Vegas Grand Prix; Russell criticised Verstappen following a collision between the pair in final practice; Verstappen taunted Russell after winning the race as the Mercedes driver crashed out
Sunday 22 November 2026 17:19, UK
Mercedes chief Toto Wolff says the "provocations" between his driver George Russell and Red Bull's Max Verstappen are a "good factor of the entertainment" in Formula 1.
Hostilities between the pair were renewed at the Las Vegas Grand Prix as a collision in final practice was followed by a war of words that threatens to continue at next weekend's Qatar Grand Prix, live on Sky Sports F1 from Friday.
After Russell had criticised Verstappen ahead of Saturday night's race in Las Vegas, the pair battled for the lead for much of the race, with Verstappen claiming victory as Russell finished ninth after a late error - made as he tried to pass his team-mate Kimi Antonelli for second - dropped the Brit down the field.
- 'He's so far below my level' - Max Verstappen taunts George Russell over error
- F1 2026 Calendar | F1 2026 Standings | F1 Gossip Column
- Got the Sky Sports app? Sign up for latest F1 alerts📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream F1 with no contract 📺
Verstappen poked fun at Russell at the time over team radio and then laid into the Mercedes driver during the post-race press conference, claiming that "he's so far below my level".
Wolff, who was speaking after the race but before Verstappen had spoken in the press conference, suggested the rivalry was good for the sport.
Asked whether it was a bad idea for Russell to engage in 'mind games' with Verstappen, Wolff replied: "They have known each other so long since karting.
"I think it's probably been a bit of cat and mouse.
"These provocations in either side is another good factor of the entertainment."
Their feud has reignited almost exactly two years on from a major blow up following the 2024 Qatar Grand Prix, which saw a remarkable war of words follow an incident in which Verstappen felt Russell had pushed unreasonably hard to get him penalised by the stewards.
'Max was a deserving winner'
The collision between the pair in final practice happened after Verstappen had overtaken Russell as the pair were both preparing for push laps, which Russell felt was in breach of a gentleman's agreement the drivers have.
The stewards gave Verstappen a warning for causing the collision, which Russell accepted as an appropriate outcome, but he insisted that "somebody's got to stand up to that guy".
Asked if he knew whether the pair had exchanged words following the incident, Wolff said: "I guess in the stewards' room there was a bit of an exchange."
Verstappen drove superbly to win the race, managing his deployment expertly to immediately regain the lead on several occasions.
Wolff, who publicly courted Verstappen after it was confirmed Lewis Hamilton was leaving Mercedes to join Ferrari, was impressed by the Dutchman's display.
"I think Max is a deserving winner [of the race]. He made no mistakes, and that's why he won the race.
"He always had a response. Some very good driving."
Formula 1 heads to the Middle East for the Qatar Grand Prix with live coverage from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1. Stream Sky Sports with NOW

items.title: 'Our Super Bowl moment' - what can WSL learn from booming US league?
items.summary:
'Our Super Bowl moment' - what can WSL learn from booming US league?
- Published
"It's turning into our Super Bowl moment."
Sarah Jones Simmer, chief operating officer of the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL), could not wait for the championship game between Washington Spirit and Kansas City Cur
items.text:
'Our Super Bowl moment' - what can WSL learn from booming US league?
- Published
"It's turning into our Super Bowl moment."
Sarah Jones Simmer, chief operating officer of the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL), could not wait for the championship game between Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current on Saturday night.
The NWSL showpiece was played out in front of a sellout crowd of more than 19,000 at Audi Field in Washington DC, with tickets retailing at more than $300 (£229).
Ultimately, the Current triumphed 2-1 to clinch their first title, condemning Spirit to an unwanted record of three lost finals in a row.
Just a few hours earlier on this side of the Atlantic, Alexia Putellas, who last month was crowned the best player in the world for the third time at the Ballon d'Or ceremony, was scoring twice for London City against Crystal Palace in front of 4,000 people in Bromley.
It is a totally unfair comparison. After all, a championship final is the type of jamboree the USA does particularly well.
Nevertheless, women's football is booming in America at the moment, with attendance figures at record highs, more franchises joining the league and club retail sales double those of 2025.
So what is behind the explosion in popularity?
And what can the Women's Super League learn from it?
A unique history of popularity
The US is the most successful nation in women's international football.
The four-time World Cup winners (1991, 1999, 2015 and 2019) and five-time Olympic gold medallists, the nation of Mia Hamm, Alex Morgan and Megan Rapinoe, has a history of winning - and the domestic game is key.
"If anything, soccer is more seen as a women's sport [in the USA]," says broadcaster Jacqui Oatley, who currently commentates on the NWSL for ESPN.
"Women have won World Cups and Olympic Games - and the men have been nowhere near as successful."
While teams in the United States became professional in 2001 - for WSL teams it was 2018 - the top flight has taken several different guises over the years.
The current NWSL kicked off in 2013 as an eight-team competition, and has since expanded to 16 franchises, with two more joining from 2028.
There is no relegation and Kansas City's victory on Saturday means the league has had eight different winners since its iteration.
As the below graph shows, the ownership picture for these sides is far more varied than in the UK, with American sides much less dependent on their male counterparts.
Indeed, Kansas City are blazing a trail. Established in December 2020, unaffiliated to a men's side and backed by ambitious owners that include Brittany Mahomes - the wife of NFL quarterback Patrick Mahomes.
Winning the championship is the crowning achievement for an ambitious franchise and such success is something independent London City hope to emulate in the UK. They are four points from the WSL summit nearly halfway through the 2026-27 season.
Kansas City were also the first club to build a bespoke stadium solely for women's football and the demand for seats at their 11,500-seater CPKC Stadium is huge. Earlier this year, Brighton announced their own purpose-built venue, planned for 2030-31.
"I think our independence is a hallmark of the league," says the NWSL's Jones Simmer.
"It is something we are very proud of. It allows us to invest in our own growth, prioritise the women's game and ensure resources are flowing to it."
It is markedly different from the UK set-up, where all WSL teams bar London City are, at least, affiliated and more often financially reliant on the men's side.
But that presents just as much of an opportunity, according to Jones Simmer.
"I know Nikki [Doucet, chief executive of the WSL] and I admire what she is building," she says.
"There's a really unique opportunity to build on the legacy of these 100-year-old men's clubs that are household names, to build women's brands that embrace the legacy but also have their own identity."
- Bespoke women's football stadiums? Why US sides are making the move 
  - Published15 March
- Brighton plan Europe's first purpose-built £80m women's stadium 
  - Published28 April
An on-pitch product that delivers
Fans of both the NWSL and the WSL are spoiled when it comes to talent.
Most of the US national team play their club football at home, with the likes of Trinity Rodman, Mallory Swanson and Rose Lavelle household names.
International stars such as Malawi's Temwa Chawinga at Kansas City, who came 10th in the 2026 Ballon d'Or rankings, and former Chelsea striker Sam Kerr further enhance the league's quality.
"Where it starts is the product on the pitch," says Jones Simmer. "The quality of football has to be incredible and we have the best players in the world.
"And they are incredibly engaging with our fans. For so many supporters, their entry point to the league is they care about a particular player."
Provided the standard of competition is present, Jones Simmer says fans will return - and her confidence is backed up by the numbers.
In 2026, the average gate for an NWSL match has been more than 11,000 - only Arsenal in the WSL consistently receive a higher attendance than that, albeit the US is almost five times more populous than the UK.
On Thursday, the final few tickets for the NWSL's showpiece were retailing at $300 on ticket site Viagogo, with Jones Simmer suggesting resale tickets could be purchased at six times market value in advance of the match.
As London City and Washington Spirit owner Michele Kang put it: "The answer could not be clearer that there is an audience for the women's game."
"It's our job to hook fans by making sure they have a great experience watching a game in a venue and that's about the quality of the product," Jones Simmer adds.
"Once folks have that experience, it's a really easy yes to tune in again.
- Families v loyal fans - women's football's attendance dilemma 
  - Published30 October
Not that quality is an issue in the WSL where high-class footballers abound. Take Putellas, goal

items.title: Purdy carves up Vikings defence as 49ers seal win in Mexico
items.summary:
San Francisco 49ers 35-10 Minnesota Vikings: Brock Purdy dismantles Vikings defence with three touchdown passes
Brock Purdy starred as San Francisco 49ers extended their season record to 9-1 with a 35-10 win against Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City; Purdy threw three touchdown passes and gained 255
items.text:
San Francisco 49ers 35-10 Minnesota Vikings: Brock Purdy dismantles Vikings defence with three touchdown passes
Brock Purdy starred as San Francisco 49ers extended their season record to 9-1 with a 35-10 win against Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City; Purdy threw three touchdown passes and gained 255 yards; watch the 2026 NFL season live on Sky Sports
Monday 23 November 2026 07:43, UK
Brock Purdy and the San Francisco 49ers offence turned what was billed as a heavyweight clash between two of the NFL’s top units into a one-sided contest, as Kyle Shanahan’s side delivered a commanding 35–10 victory in Mexico City.
Played in front of a raucous, pro-49ers crowd at Estadio Azteca, the game had been billed as a heavyweight showdown between one of the NFL's most dangerous offences, San Francisco (9ǃ), and a Minnesota Vikings (7ǅ) defence that had unsettled quarterbacks throughout the season with its aggressive blitz-heavy approach.
However, Purdy proved more than equal to the challenge, delivering an imperious performance and carving up the Minnesota defence with three touchdown passes in the first half alone.
"You have to be aggressive and don't second-guess yourself," Purdy said.
"Obviously, try to read it the best you can, but when you have players that can go get the ball, allow them to go and make plays.
"I feel like our guys did that around me today. It wasn't a one-man show. It was a really good team effort."
'Purdy was so quick'
Coordinator Brian Flores' schemes didn't work at all against the 49ers quarterback, who orchestrated three touchdown drives on the Niners' first four possessions.
"He was so good. He was quick, he was confident, he threw strikes," said tight end George Kittle, who caught two TD passes.
"He's playing with confidence, he understands the offense, he is confident in the offense. He knows the offense. When he goes out there he has this aura in the huddle."
49ers set the tone early
San Francisco headed into half-time with a commanding 28-10 lead, fuelled by Purdy's outstanding performance and a pick-six from Ji'Ayir Brown, who intercepted Kirk Cousins and returned it for a touchdown.
The 49ers set the tone from the outset, marching downfield on an impressive seven-play, 72-yard opening drive. Purdy completed all four of his passes for 55 yards, capping the possession with a 17-yard touchdown pass to George Kittle.
After being forced to punt on their second possession, San Francisco quickly regained momentum, with Purdy orchestrating touchdown drives on each of their next two possessions.
He threw an eight-yard touchdown pass to Kittle to make it 14ǉ before connecting with Mike Evans for a four-yard score to extend the lead to 21.
Brown then intercepted Cousins on the Vikings' next play from scrimmage and returned it 18 yards for a touchdown, further extending San Francisco's advantage.
The 49ers continued to impress after the break, producing a superb 98-yard touchdown drive that featured chants of "MVP!" for Purdy. The possession was capped off by Christian McCaffrey's six-yard touchdown run, effectively putting the game beyond doubt early in the fourth quarter.
Purdy finished 21 of 26 for 255 yards and a remarkable passer rating of 146, more than double the league-low 69.5 rating Minnesota's defence had allowed opponents entering the game.
Reflecting on his quarterback's performance, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said: "Seemed like he played a lot better than a lot of other guys have versus them, because not many people play that good versus that defence.
"There's a reason for that. It's a huge challenge. It was hard looking at it all week. Brock didn't get rattled, which he really never does. I think it says a lot about Brock."
However, the emphatic victory was overshadowed by a serious injury to right tackle Colton McKivitz, who broke and dislocated his left ankle during the second quarter.
McKivitz was injured at the end of a four-yard run by McCaffrey, after being caught in a collision with opposing players. The severity of the injury was immediately apparent, with team-mates visibly distressed as medical staff rushed onto the field. Left tackle Trent Williams slammed his helmet to the ground, while several 49ers players took a knee as McKivitz received treatment.
Head coach Shanahan later confirmed that the injury was similar to the one that brought linebacker Fred Warner's season to an end last October.
"That was really crushing," Shanahan said. "Colton has had an unbelievable year. It was tough to see him go down like that."
Despite the convincing victory, McKivitz's injury provided a sobering moment for San Francisco, with the team now facing the prospect of being without a key member of its offensive line.
Cousins gains unwanted NFL record
It's the Vikings' second defeat in three weeks, with Cousins also throwing a pick-six in Week Nine for the Las Vegas Raiders, before he was traded back to Minnesota.
He became the first player ever to throw a pick-six for two teams against the same opponent in a season.
Cousins went 26 for 38 for 235 yards and was unable to follow up his winning performance last week at Green Bay.
"There's no group that I have more confidence in than not only those players on defense and that coaching staff." Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said.
"There's just no really other way to put it. We just got beat tonight.
"They made some plays. I think the quarterback [Purdy] is really good and they got a bunch of really good players and they execute at a really high level."
The 49ers will look to extend their 9-1 record as they welcome Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, while the Vikings face off against the Atlanta Falcons in Minneapolis on the same night.
Stats leaders:
San Francisco 49ers
Passing: Brock Purdy 21/26, 255 yards, three touchdowns
Rushing: Christian McCaffrey 12 carries, 49 yards
Receiving: Mike Evans
Minnesota Vikings
Passing: Kirk Cousins 26/38, 235 yards, no touchdowns
Rushing: Jordan Mason 11 carries, 38 yards
Receiving: Justin Jeffe
