items.text:
One of football's most-hyped 16-year-olds - what next for JJ Gabriel?
- Published
It has been one of the biggest transfer sagas of the year - around a player who has never played competitive football.
Forward JJ Gabriel, who has recently turned 16, walked out on Manchester United in September and now has a verbal agreement to join Real Madrid.
Before even playing a senior game - barring friendlies - he has told Spanish newspaper Marca his "dream is to win the Ballon d'Or".
Gabriel's real name is Joseph Junior Andreou O'Cearuill - with Cypriot and Irish lineage - but he changed his name, reportedly for commercial purposes.
His father, London-born Joe O'Cearuill, played twice for the Republic of Ireland - but the highest level he played at club level was a loan spell with Brighton in League One and one minute in the Uefa Cup with St Patrick's Athletic. He has been actively involved in his son's career.
Gabriel was scheduled to become Manchester United's youngest ever player in the Carabao Cup against Brighton on 16 September, but had told the club he planned to leave by then.
How long will Gabriel have to wait for a first-team debut now? In the past 10 years Real have only handed two debuts to 17-year-olds and none to a 16-year-old.
When Real boss Jose Mourinho was asked about Gabriel on Friday, he said: "I don't have a feeling [about Gabriel]. I don't have a feeling with players who don't work with me."
In fact, Real have not even announced anything yet - despite Gabriel posting a 50-second video montage on social media saying goodbye to United this week.
- Madrid-bound Gabriel posts farewell Man Utd message 
  - Published5 days ago
- Why schoolboys have become a huge part of football's transfer market 
  - Published25 September
Why did Real Madrid want Gabriel?
For a while now Madrid have been getting the best young talents early and turning them into Galacticos before they cost in excess of 100m euros.
Vinicius Junior and Rodrygo came that way, then Endrick - and Gabriel is seen as the next.
It fits the policy run by Jose Angel Sanchez, the director general, and Juni Calafat, head of scouting. It is a long-term bet on one of the most promising young players in the international game.
Barcelona looked at him too, and backed away because the commissions were too high. Madrid believe in the player so much that they were willing to pay whatever it took to get the deal done.
The expectations are very high and the aim is for him to reach the first team. They want him at Castilla - Real's reserve team - but the situation right now does not allow it.
Castilla and Real Madrid C cannot sign players until January, so for the time being he is expected to play for the Juvenil - the under-18s.
Madrid also learned from the Martin Odegaard period that training with the first team while playing for the B side is a bad idea. So the plan is a spell in the B side, and when he is ready, Gabriel jumps straight into the first team.
Where Madrid are less happy is with how things have unfolded. Madrid wanted to set the timing themselves and be discreet, because they do not want problems with Manchester United and do not want to upset anyone. At Real Madrid, nobody is bigger than the club.
The idea was to keep everything quiet until January and announce it then. But with Gabriel already training in Madrid, the secret was never going to last.
The super-agent behind the move
Who is Gabriel's new agent, Ali Barat?
"Players are moving to him because his reputation is that he'll get you a move to a bigger club," one Premier League club source told BBC Sport.
Dubai-based Barat does not just consider himself a super-agent, but a "boutique" super-agent.
Born in Iran and raised in London, Barat says he fell into football almost by accident after many years in international business.
After initially working as an intermediary at low-level clubs, he founded Epic Sports in January 2020.
His major football experience before that? The football game Championship Manager.
"I was always trading players," he told ESPN this year. "I was obsessed with every single player around the world."
This was not just about living out a fantasy in the real world. Barat was drawn into the profession because of the vast sums agents can earn in commission.
What makes his agency "boutique"? Unlike the top operations which have a huge number of players on their books, Epic Sports aims to have just 22 - two for each position.
This, Barat argues, ensures there is never any conflict of interest in how he represents his players.
Barat offers bespoke management of a player's career and came to prominence in the summer of 2025 when 15 of his players moved on.
This included Dean Huijsen joining Real Madrid, Nicolas Jackson moving to Bayern Munich and Xavi Simons signing for Tottenham Hotspur. Noni Madueke left Chelsea for Arsenal, and the Gunners signed Piero Hincapie.
This led to Barat being named Golden Boy Best Agent for the second time in three years.
Yet he is largely the figurehead, with agents working on his behalf around Europe. For instance, Epic has three other agents registered with the English Football Association (FA).
Barat, who also brokered Moises Caicedo's move to Chelsea, says he uses social media, and in particular influencer Fabrizio Romano, to amplify stories and agree transfers on his terms.
He is an unashamed self-publicist, too.
"Ali Barat redefines the game again," read an Epic Sports press release to announce Jackson's loan move to Bayern. No other agency seems to promote itself in this way.
The largely AI-generated video which announced Gabriel had joined Epic Sports was right on brand.
Gabriel's deal is part of a new venture: Epic Future - and this presents an ethical problem.

Formula 1 heads to the Middle East for the last two rounds of the 2026 season with the Qatar Grand Prix hosting the penultimate event this weekend.
After a dramatic Las Vegas Grand Prix which saw 34 lead changes and Max Verstappen pull off a defensive masterclass, the F1 circus has moved to Qatar and the high-speed Lusail International Circuit.
Verstappen, who is set to finish runner-up in the Drivers' Championship behind Kimi Antonelli, won in Qatar last year after McLaren made a poor strategy call when in position for a one-two.

Like last year, there is a tyre limit which will create a minimum two-stop race with no driver allowed to do more than 27 laps on a set of tyres in the 50-lap race on Sunday.
This is due to the heavy loads which the tyres are put through in the fast corners which come one after another. The combination of this and this year's 2026 cars could create another fascinating race, particularly with high tension at the front between Mercedes and Red Bull as Verstappen and George Russell's rivalry escalated in Las Vegas.
Qualifying on Saturday is at 6pm UK time with the Qatar Grand Prix on Sunday at 4pm, all live on Sky Sports F1.
Qatar GP track - Lusail International Circuit
The 3.367-mile Lusail International Circuit joined the F1 schedule in 2021 and is one of the highest speed tracks on the calendar due to its fast, flowing corners which punish the tyres but also makes following the car in front difficult.
In the first four editions of the event, which took place when DRS was still in use, most of the overtakes came at Turn One where drivers can make moves on the outside and inside, so it will be interesting to see whether the 2026 regulations create any additional opportunities.
Qatar GP weather
As usual in Qatar, there is no rain forecast across the three days of F1 action with temperatures at around 26C for Qualifying on Saturday and the race on Sunday.

items.title: 'This cannot continue'.- Ferrari to hold fresh Leclerc-Hamilton talks after collision
items.summary:
Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc clashes 'cannot continue' after Las Vegas GP with Frederic Vasseur to speak to drivers again
Ferrari's drivers involved in costly on-track incident for second time in three races, with Leclerc given penalty in Vegas; Frederic Vasseur bemoans a "lack of respect"; watch
items.text:
Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc clashes 'cannot continue' after Las Vegas GP with Frederic Vasseur to speak to drivers again
Ferrari's drivers involved in costly on-track incident for second time in three races, with Leclerc given penalty in Vegas; Frederic Vasseur bemoans a "lack of respect"; watch every session of the Qatar GP live on Sky Sports F1 from Friday, with Sunday's race at 4pm
Sunday 22 November 2026 17:03, UK
Ferrari team boss Frederic Vasseur says he will hold further discussions with drivers Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton after their latest tangle in the Las Vegas Grand Prix, admitting such incidents "cannot continue".
After costly clashes in Monza and Mexico City earlier this season, the Ferrari drivers came together when battling over sixth place with 12 laps to go on the Strip circuit in a race dominated by slip-streaming in which the leading runners were covered by a handful of seconds for most of the race.
Leclerc attempted to overtake Hamilton with a move down the inside of Turn Seven but made contact with the Briton, who was spun around. Stewards found Leclerc at fault and handed him a 10-second penalty, which dropped him to 10th place. Hamilton finished seventh.
In an unusually-strongly worded statement in Ferrari's post-race press release, Vasseur said: "For the second time in three races, something unacceptable has happened between our drivers, and this cannot continue.
"We sent a very clear message to both drivers in Brazil, and today during the race we told them to think about the team when racing each other.
"Of course, in this kind of race you cannot freeze the positions because, with the slipstream, if you slow down, the car behind will overtake you.
"But our drivers should have handled the situation differently, as other team-mates did both in front of and behind them.
"Charles knows he made a mistake and apologised, but that doesn't change the result."
Speaking to the written media after the race, Vasseur had said: "All the other teams, they were able to overtake each other 20 times during the race.
"[Kimi] Antonelli-[George] Russell, [Oscar] Piastri-[Lando] Norris, even Isack [Hadjar] overtook Max [Verstappen].
"Honestly, you can't imagine the frustration for me but, for more importantly, for all the guys at the [team]."
What will happen next?
The situation is increasingly frustrating for Vasseur given it was only three weeks ago that he had to resolve the fallout from a first-lap battle between the drivers that likely cost the team a one-two result in Mexico.
Vasseur brought Hamilton and Leclerc together to speak four days later ahead of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, a meeting he said had "cleared the situation" and acted as "a good reset on the mindset" ahead of that weekend. The Frenchman added that they even "left my room joking together".
Immediately after Sunday's race in Las Vegas, the Ferrari team principal held an initial conversation with Leclerc having asked the Monegasque driver to see him before anything else.
Asked afterwards what they had talked about, Vasseur said: "It was not a discussion, I spoke!
"He apologised, he understands, but the result is there. That you do a mistake, you say 'it's my mistake, I'm sorry' but you did a mistake."
Asked what would happen next, Vasseur said: "I want to digest tonight [after the race] and we'll have to sit down tomorrow with both of them and to take a decision."
He added: "I want, once again, to have a discussion tomorrow. Also Charles will digest the situation and I think it's not the right place to discuss with them two minutes after the race.
"I saw Charles a bit down and I told him what I wanted to say but I'd prefer to discuss with him tomorrow about it."
'It's not a matter of rules' - Vasseur insists 'respect' the key between team-mates
The Las Vegas incident has placed renewed focus on what Vasseur will do to try and bring his drivers definitively into line, with scrutiny growing on whether Ferrari will follow the lead of other teams, such as McLaren and Mercedes, and introduce more formal 'rules of engagement' for what is allowed when in team-mate combat.
Hamilton has called for clearer policies in recent months and said after Sunday's race that "hopefully in the background they eventually figure it out".
Vasseur, however, believes the chaotic nature of Sunday's race shows that clean driving between team-mates is all about respect rather than predefined agreements.
"Honestly, it's not a matter of rules," insisted Vasseur.
"What can you do differently except that you have to respect your team-mate? In this kind of race you have to overtake the car who is in front of you. You can't stay behind, it's completely unmanageable.
"It means you just have to do it with respect when it's your team-mate, to take less risk, perhaps to come side by side and to come back behind. But you can't put it on the paper. I think the race of today [Sunday] nobody would write a scenario like this. Nobody can imagine a race like this. It means they just have to act in a professional way.
"Today it was unprofessional."

NFL 2026 playoff picture taking shape, Travis Kelce has a big day and Fernando Mendoza proves he belongs - NFL Sunday Review
NFL Sunday Review - we reflect on Week 11 in the NFL as Travis Kelce moved past Rob Gronkowski for touchdowns all-time among tight ends, Las Vegas Raiders' No 1 overall draft
items.text:
NFL 2026 playoff picture taking shape, Travis Kelce has a big day and Fernando Mendoza proves he belongs - NFL Sunday Review
NFL Sunday Review - we reflect on Week 11 in the NFL as Travis Kelce moved past Rob Gronkowski for touchdowns all-time among tight ends, Las Vegas Raiders' No 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza gave evidence he belongs and the Pittsburgh Steelers look in danger in the AFC playoff race
Monday 23 November 2026 07:14, UK
It's an oft trotted out cliché that 'football season starts after Thanksgiving'. Well, with the American holiday only three days away, the NFL playoff picture is truly starting to take shape going into the stretch run.
The San Francisco 49ers (9-1) further asserted their dominance in the NFC with a thumping 35-10 victory over the Minnesota Vikings and their much-vaunted defense in Mexico City - the final International Series game of the season - while the Buffalo Bills (9-1) share the same record as the AFC top seeds, albeit they were far less convincing in their 26-9 dispatching of the one-win Miami Dolphins.
Josh Allen threw two interceptions to allow the Dolphins to hang around until the Bills pulled away late. He and the team will need to sharpen up for their mouthwatering Thanksgiving night meeting with the Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) - live on Sky Sports NFL from 1.20am, Friday - that could ultimately end up deciding where the road to the Super Bowl runs through in the AFC.
- Latest NFL fixtures, results and UK kick-off times
- Get latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract
However, it's below the Bills and the Chiefs, and the 49ers on the other side of the conference divide, where things are really starting to get interesting.
The Denver Broncos (8-2) are also in the mix for top billing in the AFC, after claiming a sixth straight against the Las Vegas Raiders, while the Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) have the opportunity to match that mark with a Monday night victory at the Washington Commanders.
The Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) stumbled at the New York Giants (6-3-1), whose impressive victory strengthened their grip on the NFC East division, which the Dallas Cowboys (5-6) are still in the hunt for after hanging 51 on the Tennessee Titans defense.
The Jaguars' loss was far from fatal, with the Titans, along with the Indianapolis Colts and the Houston Texans all floundering in their division, though the Pittsburgh Steelers' (6-4) shock loss at the Philadelphia Eagles might well have opened the door to the latter in the race for a wildcard berth.
The Texans, who started the season 0-4, now sit 4-6 and - after a meeting with a Baltimore Ravens team in the midst of a six-game losing streak - will likely have the opportunity to match the Steelers' record when the two teams meet in a fortnight, following Pittsburgh's tricky assignment against the Broncos where they'll try to avoid dropping three in a row.
Meanwhile, back in the NFC, the greatest intrigue lies in the NFC North and the four-way battle unfolding for the division, with the Detroit Lions (8-2), Chicago Bears (8-2), Vikings (7-3) - even with their chastening loss to the Niners - and Green Bay Packers (6-4) all currently playoff bound.
Mind you, they all have the looming threat of the wildcard-hunting Los Angeles Rams (6-4) and defending Super Bowl-champion Seattle Seahawks (6-4) from the NFC West.
It makes the Thanksgiving night clash between the Lions and Bears in Detroit - live on Sky Sports NFL from 6pm, Thursday - even more crucial.
See, 'football season (really does) start at Thanksgiving'.
What we learned
The Cowboys' offense is unstoppable!
Quite literally.
Lost in amongst how historically bad their defense is - even the one-win Titans scored on five of their first six possessions, one week on from the 49ers managing to score 46 points and a staggering 584 yards against them - is how impressive their offense is, and needs to be!
The Cowboys are just the fourth team in NFL history to allow at least 20 points in each of their first 11 games and still win at least five of those games. They have allowed 20 points in 18 straight games dating back to Week 12 of last season.
But Dak Prescott threw four touchdown passes and ran in another score as Dallas found the end zone on each of their first six drives in their 51-30 thumping of the Titans to somewhat mask their continued defensive woes.
Fernando Mendoza looks the real deal.
There's still teething issues as the No 1 overall draft picks eases his way into NFL life - most notably the game-sealing pick-six he threw that ensured he starts his career with back-to-back defeats in his first two starts. But there was a lot to like too.
Mendoza and the Raiders hung with the Broncos far longer than many expected, with it being just a one-score game when the rookie QB tossed that costly interception.
Prior to that, he completed 18 of 37 passes for 267 yards and three passing touchdowns - his first in the NFL.
"I felt more comfortable than last week," Mendoza admitted afterwards. "I was able to settle in and able to see the entire field better.
"If you just do your job, your momentum is going to swing your way eventually."
Overreaction or reality?
Are the Steelers in danger of dropping out of the AFC playoff picture?
It certainly looks like they're in trouble. The 19-16 reverse in Philadelphia not only was the Eagles' first win in eight games, it was the Steelers' second straight loss, with Aaron Rodgers, who turns 43 on December 2, looking every bit his age as he limped to 95 passing yards when going 17 of 20 in the first half.
That turned into 227 yards by the end of the game after some garbage-time stat-padding, but it's looking a little rough for the Steelers, who currently occupy the seventh and final playoff berth in the AFC and have a dire run of stellar defenses to come over the next three-week stretch in the Broncos, Texans and Jaguars.

items.text:
Run macOS userspace on Linux by loading the macOS kernel into it.
xnulinux builds XNU, the open-source kernel of macOS, from Apple's published sources and runs it as a loadable kernel
module (xnu.ko) inside an unmodified arm64 Linux kernel. The hosted XNU drives the CPU and MMU directly, so macOS
processes run natively next to Linux processes on the same CPUs, with no hypervisor between them. Linux lends XNU its
memory, timers, files, network and GPU through a small interface module (fki.ko).
With a stock Ubuntu kernel, insmod xnu.ko boots a macOS 27 system disk made by Apple's own installer to the
desktop: loginwindow, WindowServer, Dock, Finder, Safari and Chrome.
One system, two userspaces. Left: a Terminal in the hosted macOS 27.2.1 (sw_vers, the Darwin kernel, launchd,
WindowServer, Dock and Finder running). Right: from that macOS, an SSH session into the Linux it runs inside (Ubuntu,
Linux 7.0, the xnu and fki modules loaded, and the insmod xnu.ko process the macOS kernel runs in).
Straight from the hosted framebuffer, 1280×800.
The hosted desktop at the end of a 30-minute stress run, rendered on the CPU (no GPU bridge).
Safari in the hosted macOS: Wikipedia's article on XNU, kernel.org and the Linux repository on GitHub, over the
hosted system's network link through Linux, with the GPU bridge on (GPU=auto).
 macOS processes (launchd, WindowServer, Safari...)    Linux processes (systemd, sshd, xnudrmd...)
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────    ────────────────────────────────────────────
 XNU (source-built, LINUX64 machine layer, kexts)  │
   ↕ linux64 host calls (xnu-patches/include/linux64_abi.h)
 xnu.ko   (APSL side: loads and runs the kernel collection)
   ↕ FKI, the foreign kernel interface (fki_*)
 fki.ko   (GPL side: CPUs, memory, faults, IPIs, files, network, host calls)
 Linux kernel (stock distro kernel, 4K pages, PAC)
- CPUs: each hosted CPU is a Linux kernel thread pinned to a Linux CPU. XNU runs on it until it calls the host
(idle, I/O, a timer); Linux keeps its own exception vectors, and fki.ko forwards the faults and user exceptions of
XNU code to XNU's handlers.
- Memory: XNU gets one physically contiguous block from Linux (CMA) and manages it with its own pmap; XNU and Linux share the user half of the address space layout (4K pages).
- Devices: kexts in kexts/ give macOS a disk (a file on the Linux side), a display (a framebuffer Linux reads), a
keyboard and pointer, an Ethernet link (a Linux network interface), a keystore and a GPU bridge.
- GPU: Metal in the hosted macOS runs on gpu/xnu-cpu-metal (metal2vulkan over Vulkan). Vulkan reaches the Linux
host's GPU through the DRM bridge (kexts/XnuDrm → host call → gpu/xnu-drm/xnudrmd → the Linux render node), using
Mesa's Venus driver; without a GPU it falls back to Mesa lavapipe on the CPU.
Working, on an Apple Silicon Mac running an arm64 Linux VM (krunkit) with 1 to 6 hosted CPUs:
- macOS 27.2.1 boots to the desktop with auto-login in 31–48 s (an Apple Virtualization macOS VM on the same Mac: 49 s).
- Apps open and quit, Spotlight and the file system work; a 30-minute stress run (40 rounds of Safari, Notes, Calculator, TextEdit, System Settings, Spotlight and a disk walk) finishes with no panic and no crash report.
- Runs as a systemd service: started at boot, stopped cleanly with the VM, restarted after a hosted-kernel panic, each
run's log kept in /var/log/xnulinux/.
- The GPU bridge gives hosted apps the host GPU (Virtio-GPU Venus (Apple M5 Max)) and is enabled by default
(GPU=auto) when a Linux render node is present, falling back to CPU rendering (GPU=off) otherwise.
What is still a stopgap is listed in docs/production.md. Notably: the OS cryptex is merged into
the system volume, AMFI is patched and SIP relaxed, and memory access is slower than a native VM (4K pages vs 16K).
- An arm64 Linux host with PAC (Apple Silicon M1 or later in a VM: krunkit for GPU access, or tart), 4K pages, 16 GB of RAM (8 GB of it reserved for the hosted kernel).
- A Mac with Xcode to make the system disk and build the GPU parts.
- A macOS 27 installation (an Apple Virtualization VM disk) of your own. No Apple binaries are in this repository or distributed by it: the kexts Apple ships, the macOS system disk and its trust cache come from your own installation.
- scripts/vm-xnu-build.sh (in the Linux VM, once): sets up the macOS-DroidVM Linux toolchain and builds XNU
(xnu-12377.121.6) natively on arm64.
- scripts/vm-xnu-rebuild.sh: applies xnu-patches/, builds the kernel and kexts/, and links the kernel collection
with Apple's kexts from your macOS installation.
- scripts/mk-macvm-disk.sh (on the Mac): turns a macOS VM disk made by Apple's installer into the hosted system's disk
and copies it into the Linux VM.
- scripts/xnulinux-boot.sh (in the Linux VM): builds fki.ko and xnu.ko against the running kernel, brings up the
network (and the GPU bridge when there is a render node) and boots the hosted system. Its console is scripts/xnu-console.sh, its screen tools/hosted/fb2png.py, input tools/hosted/xnu-input.py.
- scripts/install-service.sh (in the Linux VM): runs it as xnulinux.service, configured in /etc/xnulinux.conf (CPUs, memory, disk, GPU). On the Mac, scripts/install-krun-agent.sh keeps the VM itself running.
- GPU (optional, on the Mac): gpu/venus/build-darwin.sh builds the hosted Vulkan driver, gpu/xnu-cpu-metal/ the
Metal plugin (see its README).
The Linux side and the XNU side are kept apart by license and meet only at FKI. Every source file carries an
SPDX-License-Identifier; the license texts are in LICENSES/.
xnu.ko is on the XNU side of the line: it runs XNU's code in its own address space, so it is APSL-2.0 like XNU, and
Linux reports it as a non-GPL module (MODULE_LICENSE("Proprietary"), which taints the kernel as ZFS does). It must not
include Linux headers beyond the module ABI, call Linux functions other than fki_*, or carry Linux code. Upstream code

items.text:
Explosion on Russian ship at Libya port caused by suspected drone attack, officials say
- Published
An explosion on a Russian ship docked at Benghazi naval base was caused by a suspected drone attack, Libya's eastern government has said.
The explosion happened at dawn on Sunday, while the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia, Libya state media reported, citing the eastern government.
The statement said there were no casualties. Moscow has yet to comment.
Later on Sunday, the health ministry said it had received injured people from another vessel, a commercial ship, that was also targeted off the coast of Benghazi, state media reported. Their injuries were minor and their condition stable, the ministry said.
The UN mission in Libya expressed "serious concern" over the attacks, calling for "an immediate, independent and transparent investigation".
"Libya cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts," the UNSMIL wrote on X., external
Videos posted on social media and geolocated by BBC Verify show the ship that was struck in the morning engulfed in flames and smoke. Satellite imagery from Planet Labs PBC also shows a boat on fire at 05:47 GMT at the Benghazi port.
US-based intelligence firm Vantor collected high-resolution images that it said showed Project 20380 Steregushchiy-class corvette (Merkury) - a Russian navy ship - moored in the port on Saturday, and on Sunday showed most of the same ship capsized and sunk with only the forward bow still visible.
The eastern-based Government of National Stability (GNS) said the Russian ship - which it did not name or identify - was using the Benghazi port within the framework of an existing maritime agreement.
Sunday's incident is under investigation, and authorities are coordinating with their Russian counterparts to determine the source of the suspected attack and who is responsible for it, GNS added.
GNS condemned the attack on a ship inside a Libyan port, and called it a violation of maritime safety and an attack on their sovereignty. It said Libya was not party to the Russia-Ukraine war, or any other conflict beyond its borders.
Separately, Libya's internationally recognised government in Tripoli - the Government of National Unity (GNU) - warned against hosting foreign forces and allowing them to use facilities in a statement published by state media.
GNU said such activity raises "serious fears" about "risks that may result from involving ports and civilian facilities in activities related to external conflicts, and the resulting threat to the lives of citizens and the safety of national facilities and assets".
Libya fractured into violence and instability after its leader Muammar Gaddafi was overthrown in 2011, leading to the opposing governments.
Benghazi is more than 2,000 km (1,243 miles) away from the Russian capital Moscow.
Although it has not been officially confirmed who was behind the attack, there is little doubt, according to Jalel Harchaoui, Libya specialist at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI).
"Ukraine is the only actor brazen enough to pull something like that off," he told the BBC. "If I were to bet my own money, I would bet that it was the Ukrainians."
If confirmed, it would not be the first time Ukrainian forces had carried out an operation of this sort. In March, Russia accused Ukraine of targeting the Russian tanker Arctic Metagaz in the Mediterranean between Libya and Malta with "uncrewed sea drones" launched from the Libyan coast.
As well as having an economic impact on Russia, hampering the ability of their so-called shadow fleet of tankers to export oil and gas, attacks like this are seen as humiliating to the Kremlin, according to Harchaoui.
But it is not only Moscow that will want to react to this latest incident. The ship was in the region as part of a deal with the government of eastern Libya - allied with Khalifa Haftar, commander of the Libyan National Army.
Harchaoui said Haftar will take the attack as a personal slight. "You're going to have a response by the Haftar family. They will ask questions about who is hosting the Ukrainians."
Additional reporting by Benedict Garman and Shayan Sardarizadeh

items.title: How Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford bet big on Anthropic before its IPO
items.summary: When Notable Capital poured roughly 10% of the U.S. portion of its $1 billion-plus fund into Anthropic’s Series E, many limited partners were perplexed by the massive bet. Claude’s maker was still trailing its biggest rival, OpenAI, and DeepSeek had released its R1 model just weeks earlier, threaten
items.text:
When Notable Capital poured roughly 10% of the U.S. portion of its $1 billion-plus fund into Anthropic’s Series E, many limited partners were perplexed by the massive bet. Claude’s maker was still trailing its biggest rival, OpenAI, and DeepSeek had released its R1 model just weeks earlier, threatening to overtake closed-source competitors. Moreover, at $61.5 billion, Anthropic’s valuation was by far the highest that the predominantly early-stage venture firm had invested at in its 25-year history.
But investors at Notable, formerly known as GGV Capital before its 2024 split from its China operations, were confident in Anthropic’s future. A team that included managing partners Hans Tung and Glenn Solomon and principal Dan Cahana crunched the numbers and found that developers were increasingly favoring Claude over ChatGPT, using Claude 70% of the time, a reversal from the previous year.
“We just knew that for AI, the developer is at the center because they’re the early adopters,” Tung, a co-founder of the firm, told TechCrunch.
Having navigated the complexities of U.S.-China relations firsthand, Notable was also convinced that “mission-critical” work would always require U.S.-based, closed-source models, Tung said.
Less than two years later, Notable’s LPs are no longer questioning the outsized investment. On Wednesday, Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest IPO in history, reaching a fully diluted valuation of about $1.5 trillion before its shares began trading the next day, a paper return of roughly 15 times.
Notable is, of course, not the only firm sitting on a massive paper windfall from Anthropic. Even traditional late-stage investors, who rarely see venture-scale multiples, are set for a big win.
Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC had been researching Anthropic throughout 2024, but it didn’t make its first investment until after Chris Emanuel, head of the fund’s tech investments, met with Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao at Che Fico, an Italian restaurant in San Francisco, in early 2025. Rao helped pique Emanuel’s interest in the company by showing that model improvements were driving rising enterprise adoption. GIC then made its first investment in Anthropic’s Series F, a round announced in September 2025 at a $183 billion valuation.
“Claude Code was just released then,” Emanuel told TechCrunch. “It was very early, but even then, we could see signs that it was really popular with developers.” GIC’s conviction in the AI lab was so high that the fund later led Anthropic’s Series G alongside Coatue at a $380 billion valuation, and returned as one of the co-leads for the pre-IPO round at $965 billion. Across the three rounds, GIC invested more than $4.5 billion in Anthropic, amassing a stake equal to about 1% of the company after its IPO, according to a person familiar with GIC’s financials.
Lilian Li, who leads U.S. growth investments at Baillie Gifford, began studying Anthropic and speaking with its team nearly two years before first investing in the company’s Series F. Baillie Gifford invested in the Claude maker once it became clear that the company was “executing consistently” on its vision while generating strong revenue and “compelling gross margins,” Li told TechCrunch.
After Baillie Gifford’s initial investment, Anthropic continued to deliver on its promises, expanding into industries such as legal services and life sciences, as well as broader applications like Cowork and cybersecurity, Li said.
“It’s actually quite incredible how consistent they have been with how quickly everything’s been changing,” she added. Baillie Gifford went on to invest a total of $1.5 billion across three funding rounds, a bet that has generated substantial paper gains for the investment manager, as well as for dozens of other backers who invested at what once seemed like astronomical valuations.

items.text:
A 'wow' player - why Ngumoha is already a Liverpool game-changer
- Published
Rio Ngumoha is going to be a 'wow' player for Liverpool - and he showed everyone exactly what he is already capable of in Sunday's 4-0 win over Manchester United.
He made an outstanding assist then added a fine finish, and there is much more to come. He plays without fear so he is going to score and make many more goals the same way.
Ngumoha has only just turned 18 but he is already a game-changer, someone who gets people excited because he is so hard to stop when he is one-on-one.
Of course he can frustrate you at times too, but that's what creative and explosive wingers like him do - and it's because he is so talented that everyone wants to see an end product from him every time he gets on the ball.
There were times against United when Ngumoha did not quite deliver, but he is still so young and I would much rather see players like him take too many touches - or try too many things and fail - than be afraid to try them in the first place.
So, if he runs out of play or runs into too many players at times, because teams are doubling up on him like United were, that just shows how scared they are of him.
His ability means he occupies opposition players - Youri Tielemans was always backing up Diogo Dalot on his wing to try to help him out, but that just meant United were leaving someone else free.
Sometimes it is actually harder when you are playing out wide against 10 men because you don't get the same amount of space - United were not attacking the same way they would have done with 11, and they were sitting in more.
Yes, Ngumoha ran up the odd blind alley or got outnumbered but that is always going to happen. As he learns, and gets even better, his decision-making will improve too. He will know when to try to go past people or when to find that free man instead.
But he still showed all the bravery you want from a winger against United and, when you keep trying things the way he did, something is going to come off for you.
I look at Bradley Barcola in a similar way to Ngumoha - he can be frustrating but he tries things, and can be brilliant.
For Liverpool right now, one of the biggest positives is the competition they have in wide areas, with those two plus Victor Munoz and Cody Gakpo.
There are other areas of their squad, like left-back or central midfield, where that competition needs to improve, but I don't really worry about the wide attacking areas in the same way.
Sunday was only Ngumoha's second Premier League start of the season, and his first since the opening day.
He maybe only got his chance because Gakpo has a calf problem but, when everyone is fit, it is really exciting that they will all be thinking they have to play their best to push the manager and get in the team.
'An important day for a positive mindset'
There were plenty of other positives for Liverpool, too. All in all, Sunday could not have gone much better for them.
United made a woeful start with poor concentration and mistakes which cost them but, from there, Liverpool saw the game out well.
Just because the opposition has a man sent off early on does not mean any kind of victory is a given, let alone a 4-0 win.
Look at how United's 11 men lost to City's 10 in the Manchester derby earlier this season - we've seen many times how good teams can frustrate a side with an extra player like that.
It definitely does not mean you are going to steamroller them, but Liverpool did that and made an abundance of chances to get even more goals.
Days like this are so important for building belief in all their attacking players, especially because they were playing at home, and against their big rivals.
Up until now, it had felt like Liverpool's better days this season had come on the road, but now the pressure and expectation is off them a bit - particularly if, like Ngumoha or Florian Wirtz, you have scored and played well.
I know from experience that, the next time they go back to Anfield, they will be buzzing. You know that the fans are already with you after you've scored against United, and you feel the love a little bit more.
This is the start of a big week for Liverpool and Iraola will probably make changes against Club Brugge in Belgium on Wednesday, knowing how difficult Sunday's Merseyside derby will be.
Everton is always a tough game but I think Liverpool will enjoy their trip to Hill Dickinson Stadium, and the confidence they will have after beating United will mean they can go there with a really positive mindset.
Danny Murphy was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

PGA Tour: Rasmus Hojgaard shares lead at weather-affected RSM Classic as FedExCup Fall finale heads to Monday finish
Saturday's play was washed out by heavy rain at the RSM Classic, dragging the tournament into a Monday finish; Rasmus Hojgaard and Michael Thorbjornsen share lead heading into the final day; watch live on Monday from 3pm on Sky Sports Golf
Sunday 22 November 2026 22:43, UK
Rasmus Hojgaard holds a share of the lead heading into a weather-delayed final day of the RSM Classic, with England's Marco Penge in contention as he looks to secure his PGA Tour future.
Hojgaard entered the week 122nd in the FedExCup standings and among the players looking to break into the top 100 and remain fully exempt on the PGA Tour next season, with the Dane now in prime position to do that.
The Ryder Cup star posted a five-under 65 on the Seaside Course at Sea Island Golf Club, firing five birdies to move to 13 under alongside Michael Thorbjornsen, with Max Greyserman a shot off the pace in third.
- The RSM Classic: Latest leaderboard [external]
- Latest PGA Tour news, headlines, reports and highlights
- Get the latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract
The Dane carded back-to-back birdies from the sixth and followed a 10-foot birdie at the 12th by holing from 30 feet for another at the 16th, before closing a blemish-free day by draining a 25-footer at the par-four last to move joint-top of the leaderboard.
"Today felt very free - tomorrow's a completely different day," Hojgaard said. "I'm going to feel the nerves. I think that's what we all play for is to put ourselves in those positions, and we'll see what happens."
Penge needs at least a top-four finish to have a chance of breaking inside the top 100, with a two-under 68 keeping him within two of the lead heading into a second successive Monday finish on the PGA Tour.
Haotong Li and Max McGreevy join Penge on 11 under, while Jackson Koivun is in the group three strokes back with Denmark's Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen and Belgium's Adrien Dumont de Chassart.
The tournament was washed out by heavy rain on Saturday, leading to the final round being held on Monday. The Austin Championship last week also was delayed by rain, marking the first time since 2015 that successive PGA Tour events have been dragged into an unscheduled fifth day.
Those 51st to 60th in the FedExCup standings after this week qualify for the first two Signature Events of 2027, while those who end between 101st and 125th on the PGA Tour only receive conditional status and will be unable to feature in certain events.
The final round starts on Monday at 7.20am local time (12.20pm UK time), with a two-tee start in operation and players going out in threeballs.

A delega
items.text:
Fifa to confirm UK as host for 2035 Women's World Cup
- Published
Fifa is set to confirm on Monday that a first football World Cup will be hosted in the United Kingdom since 1966.
England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales are the only bidders to jointly stage the 2035 Women's World Cup.
A delegation will be present at Fifa's Zurich headquarters with national associations holding a specially arranged virtual meeting, and voting to ratify the co-hosts.
The tournament would involve 104 matches contested by 48 teams over 39 days.
Nineteen venues are proposed by the 'All Together' bid, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales.
Fifa's evaluation of the bid, published earlier this month, rated it 4.3 out of five. However, its contractual framework was rated 'medium risk', and the document claimed that "certain government guarantees contain material qualifications, particularly regarding tax and safety and security".
This is thought to refer to a lack of agreement over a request by Fifa for tax-free status for all football-related activities.
Fifa's bid evaluation said: "The bidder has submitted an extensive set of government support documents and contractual hosting agreements, demonstrating the commitment of the relevant authorities and stakeholders.
"However, certain government guarantees, particularly those relating to safety and security and tax, contain certain qualifications which have been duly noted in the legal evaluation.
"While certain contractual matters remain subject to further discussion, the bidder's proactive engagement with Fifa and the substantial lead-in time provide a sound basis for resolving these outstanding issues."
England hosted the women's European Championship in 2022, which the Lionesses won.
England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland are also joint hosts of the men's European Championship in 2028.
Mark Bullingham, chief executive of the Football Association, said: "Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play.
"Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations."
The English stadiums included in the 2035 bid are: Villa Park, The Amex, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Emirates Stadium, Selhurst Park, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Wembley, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, the City Ground, the Stadium of Light and Old Trafford.
If Manchester United's proposed new Old Trafford stadium does not go ahead, it will still be considered in its current form.
A further three stadiums could be added - Birmingham's new Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham's redeveloped Racecourse Ground and a potential new Chelsea ground - which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 venues.
Cardiff City Stadium and Principality Stadium the two Welsh venues.
Noel Mooney, the chief executive of the Football Association of Wales, said: "Wales has been a football nation for 150 years and we have never hosted anything on this scale. World Cup football played here, in front of Welsh children, would change what this game looks like in Wales: in the clubs, in the schools, and in the number of girls who grow up seeing a pathway into it."
Northern Ireland missed out on co-hosting the men's Euros in 2028 after the UK government said in 2024 it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in time for the tournament - but a redeveloped Windsor Park is set to stage matches in 2035.
The Irish Football Association's chief executive Patrick Nelson said the event "would be felt in every club and every age group, in every part of the country. Our young players would grow up having watched the best in the world play at home, and there is no substitute for that."
Easter Road in Edinburgh and Hampden Park in Glasgow are the Scottish venues proposed, with Scottish Football Association chief executive Ian Maxwell saying hosting the tournament would be "the most significant thing to happen to the women's and girls' game in Scotland".
He added: "The impact would go far beyond just the matches themselves. The level of investment into coaching, facilities and player pathways in the years beforehand will shape the future of the game for the generations to come."
The special meeting of Fifa's Congress is also set to approve the joint bid by Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 finals, which will be the first to feature 48 teams.

items.title: Price looking to continue trend of Grand Slam victors tasting Worlds glory
items.summary:
Gerwyn Price looking to continue trend of Grand Slam victors tasting World Darts Championship glory
Gerwyn Price won the Grand Slam of Darts with a 16-11 victory over Gian van Veen; the last four winners of the Grand Slam have gone on to win the World Darts Championship at Alexandra Palace; Price is
items.text:
Gerwyn Price looking to continue trend of Grand Slam victors tasting World Darts Championship glory
Gerwyn Price won the Grand Slam of Darts with a 16-11 victory over Gian van Veen; the last four winners of the Grand Slam have gone on to win the World Darts Championship at Alexandra Palace; Price is hoping to continue the trend
Sunday 22 November 2026 22:10, UK
An interesting trend has occurred over the last four years: The winner of the Grand Slam has gone on to win the World Darts Championship.
It started with Michael Smith back in 2022, with Luke Humphries continuing it in 2023.
Of course, Luke Littler's back-to-back triumphs in Wolverhampton in 2024 and 2025 were then followed by him lifting the Sid Waddell Trophy.
- Gerwyn Price roars to fourth Grand Slam of Darts title
- Grand Slam of Darts Final 2026 - As it happened!
- Darts in 2026: Key dates, calendar, results
- Not got Sky? Get instant access with NOW
Gerwyn Price wants to continue that in 2026.
Price roared to a 16-11 victory over Gian van Veen in the final of the Grand Slam, hitting five massive ton-plus checkouts in a confident display.
The win moves Price up to world No 3 ahead of Humphries and marks his first major title in four years.
Alexandra Palace was immediately on Price's mind following his victory and he hopes to extend the trend into a fifth year and become a two-time world champion.
"The sweet thing about this is the last couple of years, whoever won has gone on to win the World [Championship], so....," Price said after beating Van Veen.
"If that happens, then I'll take six months out!"
"I am superstitious and I believe in stuff like that," he later added.
"I hope I am not the one to break the trend."
Price has been in some form in 2026, the Grand Slam marking his fourth major final of the year but his first victory.
The Welshman has maintained he is the most consistent player across 2026 and puts part of that down to the love he now gets from the crowd.
It is a very different story from when he last won a Grand Slam title five years ago.
"How different it is, the crowd right behind me and cheering me all the way. How things can change." Price added.
"I thought these days would happen, I just didn't know when. I am glad it happened sooner rather than later.
"It definitely helps and spurs you on to come out to a crowd who is right behind you rather than against you.
"I have had that for the last two-and-a-half years and hopefully it continues.
"People have just realised I am who I am, I wear my heart on my sleeve, and I don't do things to put people off which people think I did.
"I am the most consistent. I am not saying I am the best player.
"I am full of confidence, I am in some great form. I am the most consistent across this season."
'I have now got the media off my back, not the monkey'
With the form 'The Iceman' has been in, it is remarkable it had been so long since Price had last tasted major glory back in 2022.
While he says it did not bother him, being reminded by the "media" spurred him on.
Now, the narrative changes.
"You guys [the media] were putting pressure on me and reminding me I hadn't won a tournament in a long time," Price said.
"You probably spurred me on as well so thanks.
"I keep saying I am not bothered when I lose and I stand by that.
"Obviously it hurts to lose. I have now got you off my back, not the monkey."

items.title: 'World's best could've lost 4-0' - but should Man Utd have done more at Anfield?
items.summary:
'World's best could've lost 4-0' - but should Man Utd have done more at Anfield?
- Published
Mauricio Pochettino believes even the best team in the world could have conceded four goals at Liverpool in Manchester United's circumstances - but should the struggling Red Devils have done more in another
items.text:
'World's best could've lost 4-0' - but should Man Utd have done more at Anfield?
- Published
Mauricio Pochettino believes even the best team in the world could have conceded four goals at Liverpool in Manchester United's circumstances - but should the struggling Red Devils have done more in another disappointing defeat?
The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager's first match in charge of United got off to a dreadful start as they had defender Leny Yoro sent off in the eighth minute and were 2-0 down by the 13th minute.
That left them with a mountain to climb, with Liverpool scoring twice more in the second half to secure a 4-0 win that kept United second from bottom in the table.
"Do you think that is easy?" said Pochettino of the situation that faced his new side after those disastrous opening 13 minutes.
"Even the best team in the world playing like this in this situation, in our circumstance, maybe concede the four goals or maybe more. And now what we are going to say?
"We are in a situation that this is very complicated. It's difficult, yes, but I think we fight, we made the effort, and I know how they feel now in the dressing room."
'Do you down tools and throw the towel in?'
Pochettino certainly does have a point.
Trying to win any game when reduced to 10 men in the first half is difficult. In the entire history of the Premier League Manchester United have managed it on four occasions - each of those at Old Trafford.
Indeed, in the 509 instances of a team receiving one or more red cards in the first half of a Premier League match, they have gone on to win just 88 times.
At Anfield it gets even more difficult, with Arsenal the only team to have beaten Liverpool on their own ground after a first-half dismissal.
For ex-Manchester United captain Roy Keane, though, there are ways to lose if you have a man sent off - and a 4-0 defeat was not one of them.
Speaking before Pochettino's comments, he told Sky Sports: "Are you telling me they couldn't have done better? They lose 4-0 and everyone is saying it's not too bad.
"Has a team ever got a result before with 10 men? It can be done. At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality. I can't believe what I'm hearing from people who have played for the club saying 4-0 is not too bad."
Keane was responding to his former team-mate Gary Neville, who was part of the commentary team for Sky Sports.
"That's where we've got to, where we're starting to write off 4-0 defeats at Anfield as though it's just the norm and what should be accepted," said Neville in the closing stages of the game. "The club's standards have dropped so far it's incredible."
The former England full-back added: "There'll be an element of, 'let's just forget about this game because Yoro got sent off, we've got 10 men and all that sort of stuff', but it rides into the game in midweek and from a defensive perspective I've never seen anything like this."
Keane did not agree with that view as he said: "Liverpool should have scored eight or nine. Unbelievable chances they had and everyone's coming off the pitch saying four is not too bad.
"I feel like swearing. I'll try not to. How can anyone say 4-0 is not too bad? Just because they went down to 10 men. That obviously made it a lot more difficult, but if you go down to 10 men is that it? Do you down tools and throw the towel in?"
'I've never seen anything like this' - defeat provides more defensive concern
Despite Keane's comments, a 4-0 loss at Anfield isn't unthinkable - certainly better than losing 7-0 as United did three years ago.
But in the wider context it provides more concern about a defence that is now officially the worst in Europe's top five leagues.
No other team in the Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga, Ligue 1 or Serie A has conceded more than United's 34 goals in all competitions so far this season.
It is also the second successive game they have conceded four goals, while in their last six games in all competitions they have conceded 19.
"I don't think Mauricio Pochettino can write this off," said ex-Leeds and Spurs goalkeeper Paul Robinson on BBC Radio 5 Live.
"He has to learn from it. He will have learned about his players and their attitude.
"Liverpool had 27 shots in that game. There were mitigating circumstances early in the game... but why did we get to those circumstances?
"It was because defenders were out of position again. The long ball over the top that catches Matthijs de Ligt out, the lack of communication, the tackle Leny Yoro makes and the defenders being caught out."

items.text:
Nigerian youth have shown their power in the past - why aren't they shaping this election?
- Published
Abdulhadi Dalhatu is something of a rarity in Nigeria politics.
At 38, he is among the young people seeking elected office in a country where about 80% of the population is under 40.
He hopes his age will stand in his favour as he campaigns for a seat in the state assembly in the northern Kano state in January's general elections.
"Younger people are the majority in this country and should be deciding the future," Dalhatu tells the BBC.
But Nigeria's political history suggests he faces an uphill battle.
Since the return to civilian rule in 1999, Goodluck Jonathan has been the youngest person elected president, taking office at the age of 53.
The current president, Bola Tinubu, is 74 and would be 79 by the end of a second term if he is re-elected in January.
His main challengers are also considerably older. Atiku Abubakar, seeking the presidency for the seventh time, is 79, while Peter Obi is 65.
Of the 18 presidential candidates, only one is under 40 - Moses Olusoji Adebisi, a 35-year-old businessman representing the Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA).
Although he says he is confident of winning, few Nigerians appear to know much about him and he has not been seen much on the campaign trail.
The contrast is striking in a country with one of the world's youngest populations, where young people have repeatedly demonstrated their ability to shape political debate and mobilise for change.
In the previous election, Obi, then 61, galvanised millions of young Nigerians through a social media-driven movement known as the "Obedients".
His campaign promised a break from the established political order, appealing particularly to young people struggling to find jobs and earn a decent living.
But his failure to win the presidency left many of his supporters disillusioned.
"At the time we were so hopeful, but unfortunately the result wasn't what we wanted, which made many lose hope in the system," former Obedient Nonso Chukwudi tells the BBC.
The movement had built on the momentum of the EndSars protests in 2020, which grew into one of Nigeria's biggest youth-led movement in decades.
Initially sparked by anger over police brutality, the demonstrators developed into a wider call for political reform, accountability and greater youth participation in governance.
But the protests were eventually crushed by the authorities. About 56 were reportedly killed, although officials dispute this figure, while hundreds were arrested and some had their bank accounts frozen.
Both EndSars and the Obedients demonstrated the capacity of young Nigerians to mobile around political causes.
But turning that enthusiasm into sustained electoral participation has proved much harder.
Hajara Musa, 33, is among those who have lost faith in the political system. She has no plans to register or vote in the near future.
"I just feel like things are already determined and I'll just be wasting my time. It is going to be the same people all over again," she tells the BBC.
The electoral register appears to reflect this growing disillusionment.
Although the number of registered voters has increased by 10 million to over 103 million since the last election, enrolment of those under 35 has actually fallen, by about seven million.
Young people now account for just 29% of registered voters, down from 40% in 2023.
Nigeria's electoral commission, Inec, says it has made efforts to encourage more young people to register ahead of the 2027 general elections.
This includes appointing nine ambassadors from the entertainment industry, spanning film, music and comedy, to reach younger audiences.
But the figures suggest these efforts have yet to make a significant difference.
Dalhatu says he understands the frustration but argues that young Nigerians cannot expect change, if they stay away from the political process.
"Unfortunately, many prefer to just post on social media" instead of getting involved, he says.
Of course being young does not mean you are necessarily the best candidate.
For those who want to participate, there is a formidable obstacle to getting into politics - money.
Dalhatu dreams of becoming president one day, but says he has previously had to abandon campaigns because he could not raise enough funds.
The cost of running for office in Nigeria is notoriously high.
Under the Electoral Act, presidential candidates were allowed to spend up to 5bn naira (£2.8m; $3.7m) on campaigns ahead of the 2023 elections. That spending limit has since been doubled.
The cost of nomination forms alone puts the presidency beyond the reach of most aspiring young Nigerians.
The ruling All Progressive Congress (APC), along with the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) have each set their presidential nomination fee at 100m naira ($74,000; £56,000), making it extremely hard for new challengers to emerge.
Since the return to democracy in 1999, only two parties have governed Nigeria - the PDP from 1999 to 2015 and the APC since 2015.
These parties, alongside the ADC, formed last year by politicians who had defected from the other two, have established nationwide network of branches, supporters and campaigners.
Those aspiring candidates without the financial resources to secure nomination forms and compete in the internal party contests of the main parties have little chances of becoming president.
The barriers are also evident in the National Assembly.
Not one of Nigeria's 109 senators is under 40, while only 14 of the 360 members of the House of Representatives fall into that age group.
"I have been in politics for many years and I will tell you that young people in this country lack the resources to become president," says Dalhatu, who is running under Obi's Nigeria Democratic Congress.
Fatima Zahra Umar, a young politician in the APC who has previously tried to run for a seat in the House of Representatives, agrees.

Ireland beat world champions South Africa in thriller

Ireland exacted revenge on world c
items.text:
Ireland beat world champions South Africa in thriller
- Published
Nations Championship
Ireland (17) 20
Tries: Baloucoune 2, Kelleher Con: Prendergast Pen: Prendergast
South Africa (10) 17
Try: Van den Berg, Marx Cons: Feinberg-Mngomezulu 2 Pens: Feinberg-Mngomezulu
Ireland exacted revenge on world champions South Africa with a thrilling win in Dublin after England's victory over New Zealand dashed Andy Farrell's side's hopes of reaching next weekend's Nations Championship final.
With banned South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus hosting a watchalong stream from his team's hotel, the Springboks fell to back-to-back Test defeats for the first time since November 2022 after last week's loss to France in Paris.
A losing bonus-point, however, is enough for South Africa to top the southern hemisphere table and secure a place in the final against France, who beat Argentina 45-17 later on Saturday.
Ireland, who were shown five cards during last year's 24-13 loss to the Springboks in Dublin, led at the break after two tries from Robert Baloucoune and a Ronan Kelleher score, with Morne van den Berg crossing for the visitors.
After Canan Moodie had a try ruled out early in the second half, Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast - who was cleared to play by a disciplinary panel earlier this week - stretched Ireland's lead with a penalty.
However, hooker Malcolm Marx's 57th-minute try hauled South Africa back into it before yellow cards for Ireland captain Dan Sheehan and Springbok replacement Marco van Staden - the latter upgraded to red - set up a nail-biting denouement in the final 10 minutes.
But amid a hair-raising atmosphere inside Aviva Stadium, Ireland held on for a much-needed win after six successive double-digit defeats by the Springboks, New Zealand and France.
France's win meant that Ireland had to settle for third place in the table, and they will face Australia in a fifth-place play-off at Twickenham on Friday at 20:10 GMT.
Ireland narrowly beat Australia 33-31 in Sydney in July, but the Wallabies have since had a change of head coach after Les Kiss replaced Joe Schmidt.
Ireland front up to SA after Erasmus-dominated build-up
After an explosive build-up headlined by Erasmus, who was banned for six matches on Tuesday after questioning the integrity of match officials in last week's game against France, Saturday's contest in Dublin had a lot to live up to.
But it delivered emphatically during a breathless first half as Ireland fronted up impressively to South Africa's immense physicality.
In last year's meeting in Dublin, Ireland ended a nightmarish first half with 12 players on the field as South Africa - and their mighty scrum - played the game on their terms.
Fuelled by the pain of that encounter, Ireland attacked the game with real gusto and while South Africa fly-half Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu kicked the first points of the game, Ireland bossed possession and territory for much of the opening half.
There were plenty of moments for the sold-out crowd to cheer, with perhaps the biggest roar reserved for the hosts winning a rare scrum penalty after 26 minutes.
Baloucoune was exceptional, too. In addition to faring well in the aerial battle, the rapid Ulster wing displayed his finishing skills to get Ireland on the board, slipping past Damian Willemse and touching down after being picked out by Stuart McCloskey.
While Baloucoune - who also crossed twice against Fiji last week - was denied a second try by a superb piece of last-ditch defending by Springbok number eight Cameron Hanekom, Joe McCarthy won a turnover to deny the visitors momentum.
From there, Ireland kicked to the corner and eventually worked the ball back to Baloucoune on the right, who dived over in the corner for his second.
But with both conversion attempts missed by Prendergast, Ireland were pegged back when South Africa won a penalty inside green territory, with Van den Berg dotting down off the back of a scrum.
Unlike last year, though, Ireland had the final say of the half and restored their lead when Kelleher scored off a well-worked line-out.
South Africa's frustration deepened early in the second half when Moodie's fine finish in the corner was ruled out after the replacement back was pushed into touch by Mack Hansen.
Ireland pulled further clear when Prendergast atoned for his missed kicks at goal with a penalty to put the hosts 20-10 up.
But after world player of the year Marx forced his way over with more than 20 minutes remaining, Ireland were denied a fourth try when Sheehan - in his first Test start at number eight - was held up on the line.
Sheehan was then yellow-carded at the same time as Van Staden, for a croc roll and dangerous clear-out respectively, and while South Africa pushed for a late winner, Ireland held on for a statement win.
Reacting from what looked like a conference room at his team's hotel, Erasmus slammed a table in frustration at full-time before his stream ended, spelling a miserable end to a tumultuous week for the two-time World Cup-winning coach.
Line-ups
Ireland: Keenan; Baloucoune, Henshaw, McCloskey, Hansen; Prendergast, Gibson-Park; Porter, Kelleher, Furlong, McCarthy, Beirne, Baird, Van der Flier, Sheehan (capt)

items.title: ANC fights to keep control of South Africa's key cities after election setback
items.summary:
ANC fights to keep control of South Africa's key cities after election setback
- Published
The party that has dominated South Africa for more than 30 years is in a race against time to secure power-sharing deals in most of the country's cities after a massive drop in its support in this month's loca
items.text:
ANC fights to keep control of South Africa's key cities after election setback
- Published
The party that has dominated South Africa for more than 30 years is in a race against time to secure power-sharing deals in most of the country's cities after a massive drop in its support in this month's local elections.
The African National Congress (ANC) suffered its worst result since it came to power in 1994 when South Africa transitioned from the racist apartheid system to democracy.
It won a majority in just one of the country's nine provinces, Limpopo, down from six in the last elections. It won the most votes in just two of the country's eight cities, compared with six in 2021.
At the national level, the ANC is sharing power with its long-time rival, the Democratic Alliance (DA), but while there is still no official announcement, it appears that ANC party officials do not want to replicate this at the local level.
Parties have until 27 November to negotiate and form local governments.
What happened in the local election?
While the ANC saw a massive decline in its support, it still got more votes than any other party, 31%, down from the 46% in the last local election.
But in the country's economic powerhouse, Gauteng province, which includes Johannesburg and Pretoria, the picture is different. The pro-business DA got the most votes in both cities, as well as the province's other main region, Ekurhuleni.
Nationally, the party got 25% of the vote, up from 22% five years ago.
It also retained its majority in its power base of Cape Town, and got the most votes in Nelson Mandela Bay, where Gqeberha (Port Elizabeth) is located.
The left-leaning uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party, led by former President Jacob Zuma, came third, with 10% of the vote. This is a repeat of its performance in the 2024 national election, when it came in third and became the official opposition after the DA joined the coalition government.
It emerged as the biggest party in KwaZulu-Natal province, which includes the port city of Durban, securing 34% of the vote. However, this leaves it reliant on agreeing a coalition with other parties.
The only party to secure an overall majority in a city was the DA in Cape Town.
Why is the ANC apparently choosing smaller parties over the DA?
The DA and ANC have had an uneasy alliance since they entered a coalition, along with eight other political parties, in 2024.
The two, long-standing rivals due to their opposing policies, were forced into an agreement after the ANC lost its parliamentary majority for the first time since the end of apartheid. This became known as the Government of National Unity (GNU).
Despite this, the two parties have continued to disagree on key issues, and both sides have threatened to rip up their power-sharing deal.
Ahead of the local elections, analysts predicted that the two parties could team up at municipal level, mirroring the national arrangement.
The ANC seems to have rejected this, with state broadcaster SABC reporting that most of the party's top leaders see an agreement with the DA as a last resort.
Instead, the party has been courting smaller parties to try and form councils in South Africa's cities.
In Gauteng, numerous reports point to an arrangement between the party and the anti-immigrant ActionSA, which emerged as the third largest party in the province with 17%, leaving it as a potential kingmaker.
The DA has also been trying to reach arrangements with smaller parties, and the ANC, but looks set to assume the opposition benches at least in Gauteng.
ActionSA is unlikely to work with the DA as they cannot agree on the mayoral candidates in Johannesburg and Pretoria.
Does this signal a breakdown in the relationship between the ANC and DA nationally?
It's too early to tell. Neither the ANC nor DA have spoken publicly about the future of their arrangement on a national level amid the ongoing coalition talks but the ANC's reluctance to partner with the DA in key cities points to continued strain between the two.
While the GNU has remained intact since it was formed in 2024, there have been those in the ANC who have been angered by what they view as the DA's dual role as opposition and partner in the coalition government and have pushed for the arrangement to end.
A party insider told the Daily Maverick on Sunday that a nationwide agreement to work with the DA at municipal level "was overwhelmingly rejected" at a meeting held by ANC members.
While some experts predict that the DA may have to consider its position in the coalition government given the ANC's stance, political analyst Andre Duvenhage told the BBC there was a possibility that "a lot of asymmetrical coalitions" could emerge - parties working together in one area and being in opposition elsewhere.
Another political analyst, Sandile Swana, said that any party wanting to leave the GNU over the failure to secure deals locally would be "[shooting] yourself in the foot".
Would coalition governments improve services?
This is what voters want.
The decline in the ANC's support was seen as being mainly due to high levels of corruption and a loss of confidence in its ability to provide basic services, such as electricity, water and rubbish collection.
While some attribute the increase backing for the DA to its record of competent management in municipalities under its control, some have accused it of neglecting poorer areas and townships.
But the experience of coalition governments over the past 10 years does not inspire much confidence that things will improve.
Half of the country's cities have been governed through power-sharing agreements since 2016 and these types of arrangements have often been viewed as unstable and chaotic.
As agreements collapse and new ones are forged, the delivery of basic services has often been affected.
This has been particularly evident in Gauteng, where governance in all three cities has come under scrutiny in recent years partly because of unstable governments.

items.title: Ghanaian boy killed in US 'deserved so much better', says New York Mayor Mamdani
items.summary:
Ghanaian boy killed in US 'deserved so much better', says New York Mayor Mamdani
- Published
A 15-year-old Ghanaian boy who was killed in the US last month was remembered as a hard-working student with dreams of becoming a doctor, as his father, New York City's mayor and civil rights leaders gave eu
items.text:
Ghanaian boy killed in US 'deserved so much better', says New York Mayor Mamdani
- Published
A 15-year-old Ghanaian boy who was killed in the US last month was remembered as a hard-working student with dreams of becoming a doctor, as his father, New York City's mayor and civil rights leaders gave eulogies during his funeral on Friday.
Javits Frimpong was shot and killed while walking to school in the Bronx. His death has sparked outrage in both Ghana and the US, and reignited debates about gun violence in America.
"Javits deserved so much better and so do every single one of you," Mayor Zohran Mamdani said. "Though he was only a New Yorker for a short time, New York City will forever be proud to call Javits one of our own."
Frimpong moved to the US about a year before the shooting.
"I worked hard to bring you from Ghana to America because I wanted you to have opportunities, a better future, and a chance to achieve everything that you dreamed of," his father, Thomas Frimpong, said.
His mother was granted an emergency visa from Ghana to mourn her son at Friday's funeral service, following Mamdani's lobbying of President Donald Trump earlier this month.
Frimpong was chased down and shot on 29 October. He was taken to a local hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
Police have said three teenage boys were involved in the shooting. A 17-year-old has been arrested and charged with murder, and will be tried as an adult. Police are still searching for the other two.
"Gun violence is never the answer," Ben Crump, an attorney representing the family, said at the funeral as he vowed to seek justice for Frimpong.
Ghana's government has condemned the killing and said it would follow the case closely to ensure justice was achieved.
It has urged US authorities to conduct a thorough investigation and said it was ready to provide legal and consular support to ensure the perpetrators were brought to justice.
